title: /tasks command — session task table + Gantt + agent summary (HD inline)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§2). Depends on task-cli.

## What
`/tasks` → render a **table + Gantt + agent summary** for the current session's tasks.

- Show external-to-session dependencies (tasks the session depends on but did not create).
- The diagram is sent **HD inline** (uncompressed-quality image, NOT as a file attachment).

## Why
The user wants an at-a-glance view of what the agent is working on, what's blocked, and the timeline — straight in the chat, in readable quality.

## Acceptance
- `/tasks` returns a table of session tasks + a Gantt diagram + a short agent summary.
- External deps are visually distinguished.
- The image is delivered inline at HD (use the uncompressed/photo-quality path, not a compressed thumbnail or a file blob).
- Pairs with task-cli Phase 2 (dependency graph + Gantt-render).

title: /new command — spawn a new agent session (interactive inline-button options)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§9, ref tg#3717).

## What
`/new [<model>] [<dir>] name [<task description>]` — spawn a new agent session.

- **Omitted options are chosen interactively via inline buttons.**
- Directory options = the dirs already in use + their `..` parents, all normalized + uniq + ranked LRU/MRU.
- `name` is validated with a **uniqueness warning** (warn if it collides with an existing session).

## Why
Starting a new agent session from the phone should be a couple of taps, not a memorized full command line.

## Acceptance
- `/new myname` with everything else omitted prompts model + dir via inline buttons.
- Dir candidate list is the in-use dirs + their parents, normalized, de-duplicated, LRU/MRU-ranked.
- Duplicate `name` produces a uniqueness warning.
- Built on the decisions-as-buttons flow (separate issue) — so it must honor the pending-question inject-defer rule.

comments.body:
Scoping note (investigated, deliberately NOT rushed into the daily-critical daemon this pass).

**Status: genuinely unbuilt — distinct from #85.** #85 / the forum-topics increments built the per-topic `/new` flow triggered by `forum_topic_created` (a topic message asks PATH then MODEL via buttons, spawns + binds). There is **no `/new` SLASH command** today — the daemon's `textAction` handles `/agent`, `/stop`, `/kill`, `/status` only (`features/tg-ctl/updates.ts`); `/new` is not in `BOT_COMMANDS` and not parsed. This issue is the flat-chat `/new [<model>] [<dir>] name [<task>]` command, a separate entry point.

**Reusable (already shipped):**
- `MODEL_CATALOG` / `findModel` / `spawnArgv` / `DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` (`features/tg-ctl/models.ts`) — the model-pick step.
- `buildModelKeyboard` + `recentPathChoices` + `buildPathKeyboard` (`features/tg-ctl/topics.ts`) — model + recent-path button keyboards (currently keyed to a forum `threadId`).
- The defer-while-pending machinery (#30, now closed) — the inject-defer rule this must honor.

**Net-new (the real work, why it's its own increment):**
1. A `/new [<model>] [<dir>] name [<task>]` arg parser — positional + optional, ambiguous which token is model vs dir vs name; needs care.
2. A **non-topic** pending-question state machine. The whole interactive flow today is keyed to a `TopicBinding`/`threadId`; a flat `/new` has no topic, so it needs its own pending-state store, its own callback prefixes (model/dir taps), and must route through the pending-question inject-defer guard.
3. Dir candidates = in-use dirs **+ their `..` parents**, normalized, deduped, **LRU/MRU-ranked**. `recentPathChoices` does NOT add parents and ranks by candidate order, not true LRU/MRU — a new variant.
4. **Name uniqueness warning** — validate the proposed window/session name against live tmux windows.
5. Spawn-into-a-named-window + bind for the flat path.

**Recommendation:** ship this as a focused increment with its own short design (reuse the model/path keyboards; add the flat-chat pending-state machine + the parents-aware LRU/MRU dir ranker + name-uniqueness check). It touches the daemon poll loop and a new pending-state machine, so it should NOT be bolted onto the tail of an unrelated batch. Items #58 (fixed, #91) and #30 (verified done, closed) landed this pass; #27 is the next increment.

title: tg#<id> message-ref convention + autolink (before #N PR/issue detection)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§9, ref tg#3715).

## What
Reference inbound TG messages as `tg#<id>` (NOT bare `#<id>` — that collides with PR/issue refs).

- The inbound-inject wrap should render the message id as `tg#<id>`.
- The autolink layer must recognize `tg#\d+` as a message reference and link it, **before** the PR/issue `#\d+` detection runs (otherwise `#3715` gets eaten by issue-autolink).

## Why
Bare `#3715` is ambiguous with GitHub PR/issue references; agents and the user need an unambiguous, linkable way to cite a specific inbound TG message.

## Acceptance
- Inbound messages are wrapped/rendered with a `tg#<id>` reference.
- `tg#\d+` is autolinked to the message; the matcher runs before the `#\d+` PR/issue matcher so it wins on the `tg#` prefix.
- A bare `#123` still autolinks as a PR/issue (no regression).

Note: the "— reply via tg" suffix is already removed (tg-cli main 83ac5db).

comments.body: Verified stale-open: `tg#` autolink is ALREADY fully wired into the `tg` send path (`detectMsgRefs` at tg:918, `linkifyMsgRefs`/`msgRefUrl` at tg:1170 — runs BEFORE the `#N` PR/issue pass). Inbound inject wrap renders `tg#` (features/tg-ctl/inject.ts:36). End-to-end proof via mock Bot-API (TG_API_BASE) through the real `tg` binary: - Supergroup chat (`-100…`): `see tg#3715` → `tg#3715` (tappable deep link). - Private DM: `tg#42` → styled-but-unlinked `𝒕𝒈#42` (no public per-message URL exists in a DM — correct). - Bare `#123` → NOT eaten as a msgref (stays a PR/issue ref — no regression). Tests green: `tests/autolink-msgrefs.test.ts` (28 pass). The original re-audit grepped only `features/`; the wiring lives in the top-level `tg` binary that imports it (tg:30-31). All acceptance criteria met. Closing.

title: File-excerpt attachment — quote referenced lines for path:line refs (currently broken)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§9, ref tg#3715). **Currently broken — fix.**

## What
When a message gives a file **path + line / line-range** in any common format —
`path:42`, `path:10-20`, `path#L10-L20`, etc. — attach the actual **excerpt** (the referenced lines) as a quote below the message.

## Why
A bare `foo.ts:42` reference is useless on the phone without context; quoting the referenced lines makes the reference self-contained.

- The referenced line(s) are read and rendered as a quote block under the message.
- Out-of-range / missing-file handled gracefully (no crash, a clear note).

title: Decisions-as-buttons + hanging-question inject-collision (no-expiration; DEFER inbound)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§9, ref #3706). **Has a critical bug risk — read carefully.**

## What
Verify and fix the agent question-with-options flow (tg inline tappable buttons) end-to-end.

Two coupled requirements:
1. **Decisions-as-buttons** — an agent question with options renders as inline tappable buttons; the tapped answer is routed back to the agent. Buttons should **not expire** (a decision can be answered hours later).
2. **Hanging-question inject collision (CRITICAL):** `tg-ctl` injects inbound messages into the agent's tmux pane via `send-keys`. If an interactive prompt/question is open in that pane, injected text is typed INTO the prompt and lost/corrupts it.

## Why
Without a separate answer channel, every inbound TG message while a question is pending can corrupt the agent's prompt. This is a data-loss / state-corruption bug, not a nicety.

## Acceptance
- Answers come through a **separate channel** (inline buttons → routed reply), never typed into the pane.
- While a question is pending, tg-ctl **DEFERs/queues** inbound text injection (detect the pending-question state) instead of blasting it into the pane; queued text is delivered after the question resolves.
- Inline decision buttons do not expire.
- End-to-end test: pending question + concurrent inbound message → message is queued, question answered via button, then queued message delivered intact.

Pairs with `/new` (#27).

comments.body:
Verified stale-done — all four acceptance criteria are implemented and covered by tests; the issue was simply never closed because the landing PRs referenced `tg#30` in their messages but did not use the `Closes #30` keyword.

**Acceptance vs. current `main` (commit 0976cd5):**

1. **Answers via a separate channel, never typed into the pane** — a button tap is parsed by `resolveButtonCallback` and routed back through the hook **socket** via `formatAgentHookOutput` (`features/tg-ctl/questions.ts`); it is never `send-keys`'d into the pane. Covered by `tests/ctl-buttons-integration.test.ts` ("tg-ctl ask forwards a Claude question to inline buttons and returns hook output after callback", plus stale-tap rejection, in-flight callback, etc.).

2. **While a question is pending, inbound is DEFERed (not blasted into the prompt)** — `paneHasPendingQuestion` + `shouldDeferInbound` enqueue inbound into a per-pane FIFO (`features/tg-ctl/defer.ts`), flushed on the answer via `driveFlush` (which re-checks the pane before every paste). Covered by `tests/ctl-defer-integration.test.ts`.

3. **Inline decision buttons do not expire** — a SCOPED forwarded question (the normal, answerable case) waits **indefinitely** for its Telegram answer with no timer (PR #60 / #57). The abandon bound survives ONLY for the UNSCOPED case (hook ran without `TMUX_PANE`), because an unscoped question defers ALL panes and waiting forever there would wedge routing. Covered by "a SCOPED question stays open PAST the abandon bound — no 'expired', the callback still answers it".

4. **End-to-end test (pending question + concurrent inbound → queued → answered via button → delivered intact)** — exactly this is `tests/ctl-defer-integration.test.ts`: "inbound text deferred while a question is open, flushed (and not lost) after the answer" (two concurrent inbound deferred in FIFO, answered via the inline button, both then injected in order).

**Landed incrementally across:** #35 (defer-while-waiting + buttons), #43 (plan-approval Proceed/Keep-planning buttons), #51 (unscoped defer fail-OPEN fix), #57/#60 (no-expiration for scoped questions). The inject-collision safety (the critical-bug-risk item) is the defer-while-pending machinery in (2), hardened against the follow-up-question and concurrent-flush resurface races.

The one tail this DIDN'T cover — an unscoped-question expiry silently stranding its deferred backlog — was a separate gap, tracked as #58 and just fixed in #91.

Closing as already-implemented. Reopen if a concrete acceptance gap surfaces.

title: CodeQL JS/TS: fix-or-justify 8 pre-existing TS findings (surfaced by #25 rig rollout)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP (§9). Surfaced by the new CodeQL self-gate added in PR #25 (rig rollout). These findings are in `features/**` source **untouched by #25** — they are pre-existing, not introduced by the rollout. CodeQL JS/TS self-gate currently FAILS on them, blocking #25.

## The 8 findings (CodeQL `javascript-typescript`, all level=warning)

1. `js/incomplete-multi-character-sanitization` — `features/auto-attach/transmitter.ts:51` — "string may still contain `<script`" (HTML element injection).
2. `js/incomplete-multi-character-sanitization` — `features/render/rich.ts:244` — same.
3. `js/double-escaping` — `features/auto-attach/transmitter.ts:52` — replacement may produce `&` that is double-unescaped.
4. `js/double-escaping` — `tests/table.test.ts:124` — same (test code).
5. `js/incomplete-sanitization` — `features/render/rich.ts:87` — does not escape backslash characters in the input.
6. `js/file-system-race` — `features/install-skill/install.ts:216` — file may have changed since it was checked (TOCTOU).
7. `js/file-system-race` — `features/install-skill/install.ts:246` — same (two checks).
8. `js/file-system-race` — `features/transport/telegram.ts:67` — same TOCTOU.

## Why
These are the gate working as intended on real code. They are length-counting / sanitization helpers (HTML-escape correctness) and install/transport TOCTOU races. They need a real fix or a justified, greppable `// codeql[<ruleId>]` suppression — **not** a mass suppression.

## Acceptance
- Each finding is either fixed (correct multi-char sanitization / single-pass escape / fchmod-style or open-then-stat to close the TOCTOU) or carries an inline justified `// codeql[js/<rule>]` marker with a real rationale.

title: tg-ctl forum-topics: wire the routing half (increment 3 minus spawn) — topic→pane map + inbound route + outbound message_thread_id
body:
## What's wrong / needed

The forum-topics **pure core** (spec \`docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md\`, increment 1) is merged in 2157f09: \`stepUpdates\` recognises forum-topic updates and emits \`topic-new\`/\`topic-answer\`/\`topic-route\`/\`topic-close\`/\`topic-reopen\` Actions, and \`features/tg-ctl/topics.ts\` + \`models.ts\` carry the store + lifecycle + catalog with full unit tests.

But it is **dead-wired**. The daemon (\`tg-ctl\`):
- never passes \`topicsEnabled\`/\`topicStatusOf\` into \`stepUpdates\` (so \`topicsEnabled\` defaults \`false\` — topic mode never activates),
- has **no** \`executeAction\` cases for any \`topic-*\` action,
- \`ctlPaths()\` doesn't even allocate the \`topics\` state file,
- there is no \`control.topics\` config flag to opt in.

Net: in a real forum supergroup nothing routes per-topic and outbound replies land in General (missing \`message_thread_id\`). CTO is actively asking "when will topics work".

## Scope of THIS increment (the routing half; spawn deferred)

Per spec §9, increment 2 is the spawn/bind executor and increment 3 is per-topic routing + outbound threading. Spawning a real agent on topic-create is the larger/riskier half. This issue ships the **routing half** with a clean seam for spawn:

1. \`ControlConfig.topics\` flag (default **OFF**) + config parse (\`control.topics: true\`).
2. \`CtlPaths.topics\` file allocation in \`ctlPaths()\`.
3. Poll loop passes \`topicsEnabled\` + \`topicStatusOf\` (reads the topics store) into \`stepUpdates\`.
4. \`executeAction\`:
   - \`topic-route\` → map \`threadId → paneId\` from the store, inject the already-wrapped text into THAT pane (same defer-guard + dead-pane verify as the flat path); a dead/missing pane is reported into the topic, never mis-routed to a flat agent.
   - \`topic-close\`/\`topic-reopen\` → persist the binding status transition.
   - \`topic-new\`/\`topic-answer\` → logged no-op (the **seam** for increment 2 spawn; behind the flag).
5. Outbound threading: topic-originated daemon replies/errors carry \`message_thread_id: T\`.

## Safety (load-bearing — tg-ctl is the CTO's daily 1:1 lifeline)

- Flag default OFF → poll loop passes \`topicsEnabled: false\` → \`stepUpdates\` is byte-identical to today. Existing 1:1 routing MUST be unchanged.
- Topic cases execute ONLY when the operator opts in AND a binding exists in the store.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Full \`bun test\` suite green, **including** a new integration test (mock Telegram via \`TG_API_BASE\`, mirror \`tests/ctl-defer-integration.test.ts\`) proving:
  - existing non-topic (1:1, General, no \`message_thread_id\`) routing is UNCHANGED with the flag both off and on;
  - a message in a pre-seeded **bound** topic injects into that topic's mapped pane (and NOT the flat target);
  - the daemon's outbound reply for that topic carries \`message_thread_id = T\`.
- [ ] \`topic-new\`/\`topic-answer\` are inert no-ops (seam documented) — no spawn in this PR.
- [ ] Review-gate [ok], no \`--no-verify\`.

Spec: \`docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md\` (§9 increment plan). ROADMAP #31.

title: reply to agent-B mis-delivered to agent-A: recognized route loses to the single global registration
body:
## Symptom

With two agents running (e.g. \`[3d]\` at \`%5\` and \`[rig]\` at \`%2\`), a Telegram reply to a message that **originated from \`[3d]\` (%5)** is mis-delivered to \`[rig]\` (%2). Breaks the CTO's daily multi-agent workflow. \`~/.config/tg-cli/launchd.tg-ctl.err.log\` shows \`no-agent reply: panes=0\`.

## Root cause

1. **Recognized route loses to a partial snapshot.** \`handleReplyRoute\` (tg-ctl ~1708) resolves the replied-to \`message_id\` against the routes map (\`recognizeRoute\`) and gets the correct origin pane (\`%5\`). But it only injects there if the **current** \`snapshot()\` still shows that pane hosting a same-project agent. Under launchd, \`tmux list-panes -a\` intermittently returns ZERO/partial panes (the no-locale tab-mangle class). The origin-pane check then fails and the recognized reply **falls through**.
2. **Fallthrough auto-injects into the wrong single candidate.** The fallthrough re-snapshots via \`listAgentCandidates()\`; when the snapshot is partial and only one agent pane is visible (deterministically \`[rig]\`/%2 — the last writer of the single global registration slot), \`candidates.length === 1\` silently injects the reply there. A recognized reply must never be overridden by whatever single agent happens to be visible.
3. The same recognition+fallthrough is duplicated in the history-stamp \`resolvePane\` path (tg-ctl ~2127).
4. **Unlocked routes write.** \`tg\` \`recordRoute\` (tg ~911) does read→append→write with no lock, so two concurrent agents racing a send clobber each other's route entries (last-writer-wins) — a second way the replied-to id goes missing → fallthrough.

## Acceptance criteria

- A reply to agent-B's (%5) message routes to %5 even when only agent-A (%2) is visible / registered — never to %2.
- When the origin pane is **recognized but the snapshot can't confirm it**, the daemon retries the snapshot and, if still unconfirmable, posts the agent **picker** — it never silently injects into a different pane.
- Existing single-agent reply routing + the recognized happy path still pass (regression).
- The routes write is safe under concurrent writers (no lost entries).
- Full \`bun test\` green.

title: forum-topics incr2: tg --topic <id> — agent replies thread into their own topic
body:
## Context

Forum-topics increment 1 (#54) shipped the **routing half**: inbound messages with a `message_thread_id` route into the bound topic's pane, and all DAEMON-originated output is already threaded back into the topic. But the **agent's own `tg` replies still post to General** — the outbound `tg` send has no notion of a topic. That makes topics half-useful: inbound routes correctly, but the agent's output scatters to the General topic instead of threading back under the conversation.

Spec: `docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md` §8 ("the `tg` send side learns a `--topic <T>` / `TG_TOPIC`") and §9 increment 4 / the §11 note ("`tg --topic` is still a follow-up — for now the AGENT's `tg` replies post to General unless given the thread id").

## Scope (this issue)

Add the **outbound side** only — the bounded, fully-safe piece:

1. `tg --topic <id>` flag: a positive integer `message_thread_id`. Mirrors `--reply-to` parsing/validation.
2. `TG_TOPIC` env fallback: when `--topic` is absent, read `TG_TOPIC` from the merged config-env (config `.env` → `process.env` precedence). The explicit flag wins over the env.
3. Stamp `message_thread_id` on **every** outbound send primitive (sendMessage, sendRich, sendPhoto, sendDocument, sendMediaGroup). Unlike `reply_to_message_id` (consumed after the first message so split continuations don't re-reply), the thread id rides ALL messages — every message in a topic carries the same thread id, including >4096 split continuations and album items.
4. USAGE/help text for `--topic`.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (stays deferred, with rationale)

- **Daemon-side auto-detect of the agent's bound topic** (stamp `TG_TOPIC` into the pane / route so the agent need not pass `--topic`). Requires teaching the daemon's spawn/inject path to inject the thread id into the pane env — touches the lifeline daemon's routing/spawn, deferred to the spawn increment.
- **Spawn-on-topic-create** (incr-1 author judged it too risky for one increment; still a logged no-op seam).
- **Defer-flush project-path guard** (`tg-ctl` lines ~1873-1877): a known, documented, pre-existing gap shared by the flat 1:1 path. The safe fix threads per-item project identity through the pure `DeferQueues` + `driveFlush` + 6 enqueue sites + the flush drain — too invasive in the shared lifeline flush mechanism to ship safely in the same increment as this. Stays documented; tracked for the spawn increment.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tg --topic 7 "hi"` sends `sendMessage` with `message_thread_id: 7`.
- `--topic` requires a positive integer; a missing/invalid value is a clear parse error (mirrors `--reply-to`).
- `TG_TOPIC=7 tg "hi"` threads into topic 7; an explicit `--topic` overrides `TG_TOPIC`.
- The thread id is set on EVERY message of a multi-message send (split continuations, album items) — not consumed after the first.
- With NO `--topic` and NO `TG_TOPIC`: outbound payloads are **byte-identical** to today (no `message_thread_id` key) — back-compat for the daily-critical 1:1 path.
- New tests via the `TG_API_BASE` mock + the transport-level fetch stub (mirror `tests/transport-reply.test.ts`): assert the thread id is carried, assert back-compat absence, assert it rides every primitive, mutation-verify the load-bearing "stamp on every send" guard, and a regression that flag-OFF behavior is unchanged.
- Full `bun test` green; review-gate `[ok]`.

## Does NOT touch

- `tg-ctl` daemon routing (`#54` topic-route guard, `#55` reply-misroute fix, the flat 1:1 path) — zero edits to the daemon's inbound/route code.

Closes by the PR that adds the flag + transport threading + tests.

title: forwarded question must wait indefinitely for its Telegram answer, not expire to terminal
body:
## Problem

A forwarded `tg-ctl` question (Claude `AskUserQuestion` / `ExitPlanMode` / permission prompt mirrored to a Telegram inline-button message) auto-expires **110s** after it is posted. When that timer fires the prompt is rewritten to **"expired — answer in terminal"**, the hook socket is closed with `null`, and the human can no longer answer it from Telegram — they have to switch to the terminal.

For the CTO this is the **daily-critical lifeline**. A forwarded question must stay open until either:
- the human taps an answer in Telegram (the callback arrives), **or**
- the agent process dies (the hook socket closes),

never auto-expire on a wall-clock timer.

Quote: *"такого быть не должно, надо бесконечно ждать"*.

## Why the timer exists today (the trap)

The 110s self-clearing timer is currently the mechanism that bounds the inbound **defer-while-waiting** so an open question cannot wedge routing. `paneHasPendingQuestion` defers inbound while a question is open, and its Layer-2 fail-closed arm is:

```
if (!pb.req.paneId) return true   // an UNSCOPED question defers ALL panes
```

The comment literally says *"This can NEVER wedge routing: every entry self-clears in ≤110s (the abandon timer above)"*. So a naive "remove the timer" would make an **unscoped** question defer **every** pane **forever** → the whole daemon's routing wedges. That cannot ship — it would brick the lifeline.

## Safety reconciliation (the fix)

The danger is asymmetric between scoped and unscoped questions:

- **SCOPED** question (`paneId` known): defers inbound for **only its own pane** (`pb.req.paneId === paneId`). That pane's agent is itself **blocked waiting on this very question**, so deferring its inbound starves nothing the agent would otherwise process; the queue flushes the moment the answer arrives. ⇒ **Safe to wait forever.**
- **UNSCOPED** question (`paneId` undefined — the hook subprocess ran without `TMUX_PANE`, the common Claude Code case): defers **ALL** panes via the fail-closed arm. ⇒ Waiting forever here **would wedge** every pane. The `#55` reply-route picker resolves where a *reply* is delivered — it does **not** re-scope a question's own `paneId` (a question's `paneId` is set once at creation in `hook-normalize.ts` from `env.paneId` and never reassigned). So an unscoped question is never picker-resolved to a pane and must keep a bound.

**Decision:** keep the abandon timer for the **UNSCOPED case only**; a **SCOPED** question gets **no timer** and waits indefinitely.

This lets a scoped question (the normal, answerable case) wait forever, while **no** question can wedge all-pane routing — the only kind that could (unscoped) still self-clears at the bound.

The socket-close cleanup is preserved unchanged for both kinds: if the agent process dies, the entry is removed and the pane's backlog dead-lettered, so nothing leaks on a dead socket.

## Acceptance criteria

- A scoped forwarded question stays open past the abandon bound — no "expired" edit, the inline-button callback still answers it later, and its deferred inbound flushes on the eventual answer.
- The socket-close path still cleans up a scoped question (dead-letters the backlog, frees the pane).
- An unscoped question that is never answered still self-clears at the bound and frees all-pane routing (no-wedge regression guard).
- Full `bun test` green.

title: unscoped question expiry silently strands its deferred backlog (no dead-letter notice)
body:
## Gap (pre-existing, surfaced during #57 review)

When an **UNSCOPED** forwarded question (`paneId` undefined — hook ran without `TMUX_PANE`) expires unanswered at the abandon bound, any inbound message that was **deferred behind it** (via `paneHasPendingQuestion`'s fail-closed `if (!pb.req.paneId) return true`) is **silently stranded** in the `deferred` queue:

- The expiry timer does `pending.delete` + `socket.end("null\n")` but does **not** call `onAbandon` (there is no `paneId` to dead-letter).
- `flushDeferred` is only ever triggered by a real **answer** callback — never by an expiry — so the stranded backlog is neither flushed nor dead-lettered.
- The next inbound on that pane injects directly (routing recovers — no wedge), but the earlier deferred message is lost without the user being told.

This is **pre-existing**: the old 110s timer behaved identically (`onAbandon` was gated on `req.paneId`). It was surfaced by the review of #57 (which made scoped questions wait forever and kept the bound for the unscoped case) and is asserted as current behavior in the NO-WEDGE test in `tests/ctl-defer-integration.test.ts` (`expect(injected(...).some(l => l.includes('unwedge me'))).toBe(false)`).

## Why it matters

For the **scoped** socket-close path the equivalent backlog IS dead-lettered (`onAbandon` → `notifyDeadLettered`, the user gets the "⚠️ the question expired … resend them" notice). The unscoped expiry has no such notice, so the user can silently lose a queued message.

## Possible fix

On an unscoped expiry, resolve the deferred backlog the same way the scoped paths do. The complication is that an unscoped question has no pane key, so the daemon would need to dead-letter the queue for whatever pane discovery resolved (or all panes the unscoped question could have deferred) and emit `notifyDeadLettered`. Needs care to not dead-letter a *different* live question's legitimately-queued items on the same pane.

## Acceptance

- An unscoped question that expires unanswered with a deferred backlog emits the dead-letter notice to the user (no silent loss).
- No regression to the scoped socket-close dead-letter path or the no-wedge guarantee.

title: /agent shows useless duplicate text rows + no buttons — make it an inline-keyboard picker with distinct labels
body:
## Symptom (CTO-reported)

Running bare `/agent` (no args) from Telegram prints a useless **text** list with indistinguishable rows and **no buttons**:

```
agents (address with /agent <window> <message>):
▸ 4
   4 · claude
   4 · claude
   4 · claude
```

Two problems:

1. **Useless undistinguished rows** — window 4 hosts three `claude` sessions all rendered as the bare `4 · claude`, with no way to tell them apart (multiple claude sessions run side by side: a `[rig]` one, a `[3d]` neon-text one, etc.).
2. **No buttons** — it shows plain text plus a "type `/agent <window> <message>`" instruction instead of tappable inline **buttons**. CTO: "где кнопки?" (where are the buttons?).

## What's wanted

An inline-keyboard **picker** (tappable buttons), one button per agent, each with a **distinct, useful label** so they can be told apart — the agent's cwd project dir / window name / tag, not a bare `claude` ×3. Tapping a button selects/addresses that agent, wired to the existing addressing flow.

## Root cause

- `handleAgentRoute` had a dedicated bare-`/agent` branch that built a plain-text list and `sendMessage`d it — it never used the existing `buildAgentSelectMessage` inline-keyboard picker (added for the #55 reply-route disambiguation). Hence no buttons.
- The label was `<window> · <agent>`. When a pane has no tmux window name, `listAgentCandidates` falls back to the **session name** (often the numeric window index, e.g. "4"). Three claude panes in window "4" → three identical `4 · claude` labels. `AgentCandidate` did not carry the pane cwd, so there was no distinguishing field. The three rows are three REAL distinct panes (not a discovery double-count) — purely a labeling failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bare `/agent` (multiple agents) posts an inline keyboard (NOT plain text) with one button per agent.
- [ ] Each button carries a DISTINCT, human-meaningful label (cwd project dir when window names collide / are bare).
- [ ] Genuine duplicate panes (same pane id) are deduped.
- [ ] Tapping a button routes to / addresses that agent via the existing picker machinery.
- [ ] The #55 inline-keyboard picker (`buildAgentSelectMessage` + `pendingAgent` + `tga:` callbacks) is REUSED, not reimplemented.
- [ ] Full `bun test` green; spec `docs/specs/agent-addressing.md` updated.

title: /agent picker: drop the redundant text list + ▸window header — buttons only
body:
After the #62 picker shipped, the project-distinct LABELS are good, but the picker message renders BOTH a text list AND the inline-keyboard buttons:

```
Pick an agent to address:
▸ 4
   hyperide · claude
   agent-tools · claude
   neon-text · claude
```

…with the buttons rendered below by Telegram.

CTO complaint:
- "что за треугольник и 4?" — the `▸ 4` window-group header (the tmux window the panes live in) is confusing noise.
- "Зачем текст дублирует кнопки? Достаточно кнопок" — the per-agent text list duplicates the buttons; buttons are enough.

Wanted: the picker message = a short prompt (e.g. "Pick an agent:") + the inline-keyboard BUTTONS. No `▸ <window>` group header, no per-agent text lines (the buttons already carry the distinct labels).

`buildAgentSelectMessage` (features/tg-ctl/agent-match.ts) is shared by BOTH the bare `/agent` picker AND the #55 reply-route disambiguation picker — both only consume `payload.text` + `payload.reply_markup`, so buttons-only is fine for both.

title: ask-forward silently drops a question when the registration doesn't match (no log line)
body:
## Symptom

A Claude Code **AskUserQuestion** raised in one session (e.g. the \`ext-test-projects\` / \"ext / hyper-saas\" session, cwd \`/Users/ultra/work/ext-test-projects\`) was **never forwarded to Telegram**. The CTO answered it in the local Claude Code harness UI (the 3-option \"Origin wins / Keep local / Merge both\" picker is the *harness* AskUserQuestion UI, NOT a Telegram message). Nothing reached Telegram, and **nothing was logged** — a silent non-forward.

## Corrected framing

A prior diagnosis wrongly assumed the screenshot was a \`tg --tag decision\` text report and the issue was buttons-vs-text. That was wrong. The question never reached tg at all. The real path that failed is the **ask-hook → daemon → Telegram forward**.

## Root cause

tg-ctl keeps a **single** registration file (\`tg-ctl.<botId>.registration.json\`) naming the one pane/cwd that currently owns the inline keyboard. At the time, it was registered to a **different** session:

\`\`\`json
{"registeredAt":...,"paneId":"%2","cwd":"/Users/ultra/xp/tg-cli"}
\`\`\`

When the ext session's \`tg-ctl ask\` hook fired, \`registrationAllowsHook\` (features/tg-ctl/questions.ts:90) returned **false** (its pane/cwd didn't match the registered \`%2\` / \`/Users/ultra/xp/tg-cli\`). \`handleHookSocketLine\` (tg-ctl:1133) then did a silent \`socket.end(\"null\")\` — **no log line at all** — and the harness fell back to its local UI. So the operator had zero signal that a question was dropped, or why.

## The logging gap (the primary fix)

Every non-forward branch in \`handleHookSocketLine\` and every \`null\`-return in \`askDaemon\` / \`normalizeHookPayload\` is **silent** (no \`log()\` call):

| Branch | Location | Logs today? |
|---|---|---|
| daemon re-parse rejects line | tg-ctl:1128 | no |
| **registration mismatch/absent** | **tg-ctl:1133** | **no** ← the one that bit us |
| not forwardable (agent/kind) | tg-ctl:1138 | no (sends a TG notice, but no log) |
| duplicate in-flight key | tg-ctl:1147 | no |
| TG send failed → abandon | tg-ctl:1209 | only the low-level \`sendMessage failed\` |
| client-side give-up (no daemon / null reply / unsupported payload) | askDaemon tg-ctl:1262, normalizeHookPayload null | no |

There is already positive precedent for this kind of observability: the inbound reply path logs \`no-agent reply: panes=0 …\` (tg-ctl). The **outbound** ask-forward path has no equivalent.

## Fix

1. Make **every** ask-forward attempt + outcome a clear, greppable \`log()\` line: a question arrived (request id / agent / kind / pane / cwd), and either **posted to Telegram** or **dropped — with the distinct reason** (not-registered / not-forwardable / duplicate / send-failed / unsupported-payload). No more silent \`socket.end(\"null\")\`.
2. tg-ctl is the CTO's daily lifeline — the happy-path forward (post buttons, return hook output) must stay intact.
3. Tests (mock Telegram via \`TG_API_BASE\`): assert each non-forward branch now emits its distinct diagnostic; the happy path still posts buttons + returns hook output.

## Underlying provisioning note

The deeper cause is that only one session is registered at a time. If the ext session's Claude Code didn't run \`tg start\` (or another session re-registered after it), its questions can't forward by design. The tg-ctl-side deliverable here is the **logging + diagnostic** so this is visible; the registration/provisioning model is tracked separately.

title: per-pane registration set: every live session's questions forward (kill the single-registration limit)
body:
## Problem

tg-ctl keeps ONE global registration file (`tg-ctl.<botId>.registration.json`) naming a single pane/cwd. Every `tg` send from a session with a detected agent (`MODEL`) auto-runs `tg-ctl start --pane <TMUX_PANE> --cwd <cwd>`, which **overwrites** that single file (`startLauncher`, tg-ctl ~735). So the registration migrates to whichever session last ran `tg start`.

Consequence: an `AskUserQuestion` (or permission prompt) from any OTHER live session fails `registrationAllowsHook` (`features/tg-ctl/questions.ts` ~90) → the daemon drops the forward (now logged as `ask-forward dropped: reason=not-registered`, #66). The CTO runs MULTIPLE sessions concurrently ([rig], [3d], ext-test-projects, hyperide) and keeps hitting this — questions from non-registered sessions never reach Telegram.

This single-registration model is the common root of the reply-route fix (#55) and the misroute work.

## Fix — per-pane registration SET

Replace the single registration with a per-pane registration **store** (a JSON array keyed by `paneId`), so multiple sessions register concurrently without clobbering each other.

- Each session's `tg start` upserts ITS OWN pane/cwd as one entry (keyed by `paneId`), instead of overwriting one global file. A session re-running `tg start` updates only its own entry.
- Entries for dead panes are pruned by liveness (the pane no longer appears in the live tmux snapshot), mirroring the routes-lock PID-liveness discipline.
- `registrationAllowsHook` / `hookMatchesRegistration`: a hook question is allowed/forwarded when ITS pane (the asking session's `TMUX_PANE`, already in the ask payload) matches ANY registered entry — so EVERY registered session's questions forward, scoped to that session's pane.
- The forward posts the question scoped to the ASKING pane (already has `req.paneId`); the answer routes back into THAT pane (held socket — unchanged per-question).
- Inbound/reply routing (`pickTargetPane`, `handleReplyRoute`): tier-1 (single global registration) becomes "match among the registered set". Preserve:
  - the recognized-reply-beats-registration guarantee (#55),
  - the unscoped-question fail-closed (#49),
  - a FRESH non-reply inbound with multiple registered agents stays ambiguous → existing picker/fail-closed (disambiguation is forum-topics #31's job, not this).

## Back-compat

The new daemon reads the OLD single-registration file shape and migrates it into the set on first read, so a running daemon's live registration isn't lost across the deploy/restart.

## Tests

Mock Telegram via `TG_API_BASE`, mirroring the registration/forward/route integration tests:
- TWO sessions registered concurrently — a question from EITHER forwards (both post buttons, scoped to the right pane).
- A session re-registering doesn't drop the other.
- A dead pane's entry is pruned.
- Recognized reply-routing (#55) + unscoped fail-closed (#49) STILL hold.
- Single-session happy path byte-identical.

title: self-provision the bot command menu via setMyCommands on startup
body:
## Problem

The tg-ctl bot handles slash-commands (`/agent`, `/stop`, `/kill`, `/status`) but never registers them with Telegram via `setMyCommands`. As a result they do NOT appear in the Telegram client's command menu (the "/" autocomplete or the menu button), so the user has to remember and type them blind.

## Ask (CTO)

> "/agent и другие команды добавь в меню бота, бот должен сам провайдить свои команды."

The bot should publish its own command list to Telegram on startup.

## Scope

On daemon startup (`runDaemon`), POST `setMyCommands` with the user-invocable command list:

- `/agent` — route a message to a specific agent (fuzzy match, else picker)
- `/stop` — interrupt the current agent turn (Escape); session survives
- `/kill` — end the agent session (SIGINT)
- `/status` — report daemon state

Only the bot's OWN commands are registered — pass-through slashes (`/compact`, `/clear`, …) that go verbatim to the harness are NOT the bot's commands and must not be published.

Constraints (Telegram): command names lowercase, no leading `/`, `[a-z0-9_]`, <=32 chars; descriptions 1-256 chars; <=100 commands.

## Resilience

A failed `setMyCommands` (network/API error) MUST NOT crash or block daemon startup — log and continue. The daemon's core job is routing, not the menu.

## Acceptance

- Startup POSTs `setMyCommands` with the expected list (asserted in an integration test against the Bot-API fake).
- A failing `setMyCommands` does not crash startup.
- A guard test keeps the published list in sync with the actually-handled commands, so a newly-handled command can't silently miss the menu.
- Full `bun test` green.

title: test hygiene: ctl-multi-session-forward integration leaks detached tg-ctl daemons
body:
## Finding (deferred from #69)

`tests/ctl-multi-session-forward-integration.test.ts` calls `tg-ctl start` (the "re-register" and "two concurrent starts" cases). `startLauncher` ALWAYS spawns a detached `tg-ctl run` daemon (unref'd) regardless of whether one already holds the flock. The flock makes the duplicate exit ~immediately, BUT on a busy machine a few escape the test's `afterAll` (which only kills the `procs[]` it tracked, not the detached grandchildren), leaving daemons in `/T/tgctl-multisess-*` temp dirs that idle-exit only after 30 min.

Observed during #69: 3 leftover `tg-ctl run` daemons in temp dirs (harmless — mock token, isolated config — but untidy). Reaped manually.

## Fix

In the test's `afterAll`, also kill any daemon whose config dir is `cfgDir`:
- read `${cfgDir}/tg-ctl.123.pid` and SIGKILL it, OR
- `pkill -f "TG_CTL_CONFIG_DIR=${cfgDir}"` style sweep of stragglers.

Low priority — test-only, no production impact, daemons self-expire.

title: tg --tag answer must require --reply-to; hidden terminal-only bypass, not in help
body:
## Problem

`tg --tag answer` (an ANSWER) must reply to a SPECIFIC inbound Telegram message — it must require `--reply-to <message_id>`. An answer with no reply target reads as a reply that isn't one.

There is ONE legitimate exception: the question originated in the TERMINAL (the Claude/agent harness), where there simply is no Telegram message id to reply to. In that case tg may tell the user HOW to bypass the requirement — but that bypass must NOT be discoverable in `--help`/usage; it must only be surfaced in the specific error when `--tag answer` lacks `--reply-to`.

## Current state (origin/main)

- The answer-gate already exists (`features/cli/args.ts`): `--tag answer` without `--reply-to` errors with exit 1.
- BUT the error offers "pick a different tag" as the escape — which defeats the purpose (it stops being an answer). There is NO terminal-only bypass.
- No bypass flag exists today.

## Asks

1. `--tag answer` WITHOUT `--reply-to` → FAIL with a clear, actionable error.
2. Add an EXPLICIT, HIDDEN bypass flag for the terminal-question case (`--terminal-question`): permits `--tag answer` without `--reply-to` when the answered question originated in the terminal and no Telegram message id exists.
3. The bypass flag must be ABSENT from `--help`/usage. Only the ERROR message (when `--tag answer` lacks `--reply-to`) mentions it, framed strictly as the terminal-origin escape.

## Tests

- `--tag answer` w/o `--reply-to` → clear error mentioning the bypass.
- `--tag answer` WITH `--reply-to` → sends.
- bypass flag permits answer-without-reply-to.
- bypass flag is ABSENT from `--help`/usage (asserted).
- `--help` still lists the normal flags.

title: tg-ctl: ambiguous/gone target dumps plain text instead of the tappable agent picker
body:
## Problem

When a Telegram route/reply cannot resolve to a single agent — or the agent it was addressed to is GONE — the tg-ctl daemon dumps a **plain-text** "ambiguous target — candidates: …" list:

```
ambiguous target — candidates:
4:1 %0 (claude, /Users/ultra/work/hyperide)
4:2 %2 (claude, /Users/ultra/xp/agent-tools)
```

The CTO (daily-critical user) wants the same **inline-keyboard picker** `/agent` already posts: tappable buttons, one per live candidate, distinct project labels.

## Two cases

1. **AMBIGUOUS** (several live agents, none clearly the one) → post the agent picker ("Pick an agent:" / "Route to which agent?") + buttons. Tapping routes the pending text to the chosen pane.
2. **TARGET GONE** (a reply whose recorded origin pane is no longer a live, same-project agent) → post the picker WITH a notice: "That agent (<label>) is no longer running — pick a live one:" + buttons for the live agents.

## Out of scope / unchanged

- The recognized-single-target happy path (#55) still injects directly — picker only on genuine ambiguity / gone target.
- The `tg-ctl status` terminal diagnostic keeps its text candidate list (a terminal can't render tappable buttons).

## Acceptance

- Ambiguous route posts an inline keyboard (no "candidates:" / "ambiguous target" text), one button per live candidate, distinct labels, `tga:` callback data.
- Reply to a gone agent posts the picker WITH the "no longer running" notice naming the gone agent.
- Tapping a button routes to the chosen pane.
- Single recognized target still injects directly (no picker).
- Full `bun test` green.

title: no-reply auto-bind to last-active agent + /agent picker uses tmux window names not cwd
body:
Two tg-ctl routing/picker fixes (CTO daily-critical lifeline).

**Context:** Direct reply routing works (#55). Two follow-up gaps the CTO reported with screenshots.

## (B) No-reply auto-bind broken
When the CTO sends a message WITHOUT replying, it should auto-bind to the agent of the LAST message (the most-recently-active agent), but instead it falls to `ambiguous target — candidates: …`.

**Fix:** a non-reply inbound that would otherwise be ambiguous binds to the most-recently-active agent (the pane whose outbound activity is most recent, from routes.json LRU/MRU) as the default — instead of declaring ambiguity. Precedence: (1) recognized reply route (#55), (2) this no-reply auto-bind, (3) the ambiguous button-picker ONLY when there is genuinely no recent agent to bind to. Auto-bind should REDUCE how often the picker fires, not replace it. Keep the unscoped fail-closed safety (#49) where a bind genuinely can't be determined.

## (C) /agent picker shows directories, not window names
The picker labels show the cwd basename (`hyperide · claude`, `agent-tools · claude`) but the CTO wants the tmux WINDOW NAME he set (`rig`, `3d`). `/agent` "не знает имен окон и пишет только директории".

**Fix:** picker labels (both `/agent` and the ambiguous picker) show `<window-name> · <model>` using the real tmux window name (`#{window_name}`/`#W`), falling back to the cwd basename only when the window name is unhelpful (a bare default like `zsh`/a number/the agent's own name).

## Tests
Mock Telegram via TG_API_BASE + a fake tmux fleet: a non-reply inbound with a known most-recent agent binds to it (no picker); a reply still routes by reply (#55); no recent agent → still falls to picker/fail-closed; picker label shows the WINDOW NAME not the cwd; fallback to cwd when the window name is a default.

title: no-reply inbound binds to the last-message agent (simplify the MRU machinery); fix the regression
body:
## Problem

A non-reply Telegram message — one sent WITHOUT replying to a specific agent's message — should simply land on the agent of the **last message in the chat** (the most-recently-active agent that posted). This used to Just Work, but a recent stack regressed it: a fresh non-reply message now pops an agent **picker** instead of routing to the last-active agent.

## Root cause (regression)

Before #69 the daemon used `pickTargetPane(panes, procs, single-reg, …)`. The registration file held ONE entry — whichever agent ran `tg start` last — so Tier 1 (registration paneId) resolved to a SINGLE pane and a non-reply message went straight there. That was the simple "last agent" behavior.

- **#69** switched to `pickTargetPaneFromSet(panes, procs, regs[], …)`: now EVERY live agent session is in the registration SET, so Tier 1 matches MULTIPLE registered panes → returns `ambiguous`. The simple single-target resolution was lost.
- **#76** turned the `ambiguous` result into a tappable picker.
- **#77** bolted `resolveAmbiguousByActivity` (a per-pane LRU/MRU map built from `aggregateUsage` over routes.json) on top to recover — but it only fires when (a) the base result is `ambiguous`, (b) routes.json has history, and (c) there is a UNIQUE most-recent pane. In practice it does not resolve (empty/insufficient history → picker), and the per-pane aggregation machinery is far more complex than the problem needs.

## The simple semantics we want

- Track the LAST OUTBOUND message's origin pane — a single "who posted last" value (the newest entry in routes.json by send time).
- A NON-REPLY inbound binds to that last-message agent as the PRIMARY behavior, not narrowly gated behind "ambiguous".
- Precedence: (1) a recognized reply route (#55) wins; (2) else bind to the last-message agent (when it is still a live candidate); (3) only if there is NO last-message agent (no history, or it's gone) fall to the #76 picker.
- Simplify `resolveAmbiguousByActivity`/`aggregateUsage` to the direct last-message-pane lookup (keep behavior, cut the machinery).
- Keep the safety: `/kill`/`/stop` (destructive) must NOT auto-bind to a guessed agent (#77's scoping); reply-routing (#55) and the unscoped fail-closed (#49) stay intact.

## Acceptance

- A non-reply inbound after agent X posted last → binds to X, no picker.
- A newer post from Y flips the bind to Y.
- A reply still routes by reply (#55).
- No last message at all → picker (#76).
- `/kill` never auto-binds.
- Full `bun test` green.

title: tg VERSION literal (1.15.0) has DRIFTED from package.json (1.0.0) — derive it dynamically
body:
## Problem

`features/cli/version.ts` declares `export const VERSION = '1.15.0'` as a hardcoded literal, but `package.json` says `"version": "1.0.0"` — the two have DRIFTED. tg's `--version` does append a runtime git short-hash (so it is partly a freshness signal, better than the python CLIs), but the declared `VERSION` literal is a hand-maintained copy that already disagrees with the manifest.

This is the drift variant of the bump-version-on-release anti-pattern (agent-tools#98): two sources of truth, kept in sync by hand, already out of sync.

## Fix

1. Make `VERSION` read from `package.json` (`require('../../package.json').version` / a JSON read at runtime) so there is ONE source of truth and it cannot drift.
2. Reconcile package.json's `version` to the intended current value, then bump it on every release (agent-tools skill `bump-version-on-release`; semver patch/minor/major).
3. tg ships a package.json, so the agent-tools version-bump ship gate (agent-tools#98 / PR agent-tools#99) will enforce step 2 once provisioned.

Follow-up from agent-tools#98.

title: integration tests leak daemon processes → flaky no-agent; guarantee teardown
body:
## Problem

The `tests/ctl-*-integration.test.ts` suite spawns real `tg-ctl run` daemons (and, via `tg-ctl start`, detached `run` grandchildren) against a mock Telegram + temp-dir socket. Several agents this session had to manually `pkill` stray test daemons. A leaked daemon from a deleted-worktree binary, holding a temp socket and competing for the singleton flock, is exactly the kind of thing that causes flaky `no agent` / intermittent routing failures.

### Leak vectors found

1. **spawn-before-track gap (every `startDaemon` helper).** The helper did `Bun.spawn([... 'run'])` and THEN `expect(socketExists).toBe(true)`. When that assert throws (socket never appeared), the spawned daemon was not yet pushed to `procs[]` → never killed. Any throw between spawn and the `procs.push` leaks the daemon.
2. **detached grandchild (multi-session-forward, = #70).** `tg-ctl start` always spawns an unref'd detached `tg-ctl run`. The flock makes a duplicate exit fast, BUT the grandchild's flock+pid-write is async and can come up AFTER `afterAll` killed the main daemon (freeing the flock) — so a late grandchild acquires the flock and survives. `procs[]` only ever held the `start` launcher, never the grandchild.
3. **timing flake (`ctl-buttons-failure`).** Two tests asserted `Date.now() - t0 < 1500` while a mock op blocked 3000ms — proving the ask returns before the slow op. The 1500ms budget is too tight under full-suite parallel load (cold `bun` subprocess spawn + IPC can exceed it) → 1 pass / 2 fail across identical runs.

### Consequence
Stray temp-dir daemons idle-exit only after 30 min; in the meantime they compete for the singleton socket lock and surface as flaky `no agent` intermittents.

## Fix
- New shared helper `tests/helpers/daemon-lifecycle.ts`: a registry that tracks the daemon + its temp cfgDir **before** the socket wait (closes vector 1), a guaranteed `reapDaemons` teardown that kills tracked procs + awaits exit, plus a **scoped backstop** that reaps any daemon recorded in `<cfgDir>/tg-ctl.<botId>.pid` (covers vectors 1 and 2). The backstop is keyed on the temp cfgDir's own pid file, so it can NEVER touch the real daemon (a non-temp config dir).
- For the detached-grandchild race: `awaitDetachedStartsSettled` lets every grandchild reach (and lose) the flock while the main daemon still holds it, before teardown — plus a settle-loop in `reapCfgDir` as the backstop.
- De-flake the two timing tests deterministically: assert a flag that flips only after the slow 3s op completes is still false at ask-exit, instead of a wall-clock budget.

## Acceptance
- Full `bun test` green.
- After the suite, `pgrep -f tg-ctl` returns to baseline (no temp-dir strays).
- A failing test still gets its daemon reaped (proven with a deliberately-throwing test).

Supersedes #70 (its narrower multi-session detached-daemon case is included here).

title: forum-topics: spawn an agent on forum_topic_created (the /new flow trigger — spec increment 2)
body:
From the ecosystem ROADMAP / `docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md` §5, §9 **increment 2** (the spawn + bind executor). The routing half (#54/#56/#61) and the pure foundation (state machine + model catalog + slugifier) already landed; the entrypoint `topic-new`/`topic-answer` actions were logged no-ops behind the `control.topics` flag. This is the SPAWN-ON-TOPIC-CREATE trigger of the `/new` flow tracked in #27, scoped to forum topics.

## What
When a Telegram **forum topic is created** (`forum_topic_created`), the daemon runs the interactive `/new` flow and spins up a fresh agent bound to that topic:

1. `forum_topic_created` → `awaiting-path` binding + a "which directory?" prompt posted into the topic.
2. A path message → validated (must exist + be a directory) → `awaiting-model` + a model-catalog inline-button keyboard (`tgm:<threadId>:<modelId>`). A bad path re-asks, never advances.
3. A model button tap → `tmux new-window -c <path> -P -F '#{pane_id}' -- <catalog argv>` → bind the returned pane → `bound` + a "spawned <model> in <path>" confirmation. Messages in the topic then route to that pane (#54 routing).

The topic NAME is only the tmux-window slug (`slugifyTopicName`); path + model come from the interactive flow (per the spec — NOT encoded in the topic name).

## Safety (daily-critical daemon)
- Every spawn step is exception-guarded — a bad path / missing tmux / spawn error NEVER throws into the poll loop; it posts a human-readable error into the topic and leaves the binding mid-flow for a retry.
- Idempotent: an already-`bound` topic refuses a second spawn; a duplicate `forum_topic_created` is filtered in `stepUpdates`, so a restart / dup can't double-spawn.
- Gated behind `control.topics` (default OFF) → 1:1 behaviour byte-identical.

## Acceptance
- A valid create → path → model-tap spawns exactly one agent, binds the topic, window = the topic-name slug, model argv from the catalog.
- A malformed path posts an error, no spawn; the daemon keeps polling.
- A spawn failure is caught (binding stays awaiting-model, daemon survives).
- A duplicate create does not double-spawn.
- `control.topics: false` → no binding, no spawn.
- Full `bun test` green.

Refs #27.

title: tg-ctl forum-topics increment-4 polish: recent-path buttons, clear model keyboard, re-spawn on dead pane, crash-orphan reconcile
body:
Increment-4 lifecycle polish for forum-topics spawn (deferred from #85; spec `docs/specs/tg-forum-topics.md` §9 increment 4). Refs #31, #85.

The #85 spawn state machine landed (`forum_topic_created` → awaiting-path → model buttons → `tmux new-window` → bind → route). #85 explicitly deferred four bounded items to increment 4:

1. **Recent-repo path buttons** on the awaiting-path step. Today the working directory is free-text only. Offer inline buttons for recent/known project paths (derived from the routes store `cwd` + per-pane registration cwds), keeping the free-text fallback. The offered paths are persisted on the binding so a tap unambiguously recovers the chosen path (callback_data is too small for a full path).

2. **Clear the model keyboard on bind.** The `topic-model` callback carries the prompt `messageId` but never `editMessageReplyMarkup`s it away after the agent is spawned, so the stale model buttons stay tappable (harmless — the `bound`-guard refuses them, but visually wrong). Remove the keyboard on bind.

3. **Re-spawn on a dead/closed pane.** A message to a topic whose bound pane was killed currently marks the binding `closed` and tells the human to "recreate the topic" (silent dead-end for routing). Detect the dead pane and offer a one-tap **Re-spawn** (re-using the retained path + model) instead.

4. **Crash-window orphan reconcile on startup.** Between a successful `tmux new-window` and persisting the `bound` write, a daemon crash orphans a live window with an `awaiting-model` binding; a later re-tap then spawns a SECOND agent (the "restart can't double-spawn" guarantee only covers `bound` topics). On startup, scan non-bound bindings whose topic-slug window already hosts a live agent → re-bind (reconcile) instead of orphaning; and mark `bound` bindings whose pane is gone as `closed`.

## Safety (this is the CTO's daily-critical lifeline daemon)
- Fail-soft: nothing throws into the poll loop.
- Gated behind `control.topics` (default OFF → 1:1 byte-identical when off).
- Preserve #85 spawn + #55 reply-routing + #69 per-pane registration; no 1:1 regression.

## Acceptance
- Recent-path buttons offered on awaiting-path; a tap fills the path and advances to awaiting-model; free-text still works.
- Model keyboard cleared (editMessageReplyMarkup) after bind.
- A message to a topic with a dead bound pane offers Re-spawn (not a dead-end); the tap re-spawns with the retained path/model and re-binds.
- A crash-orphaned topic-slug window is reconciled (re-bound) on startup; a `bound` binding with a gone pane is marked closed.
- topics-flag-off → all of the above are no-ops, 1:1 unchanged.
- Full `bun test` green.

title: tg-ctl status: autostart shows 'NOT enabled' when daemon is supervised by an external launchd job
body:
## Bug

`tg-ctl status` reports `autostart: NOT enabled` even though the daemon IS autostarted on boot by an external launchd job.

On this machine the daemon is supervised by `ai.hyperide.tg-ctl` (a LaunchAgent at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hyperide.tg-ctl.plist`, `KeepAlive=true`, `RunAtLoad=true`) whose `ProgramArguments` is `bun /Users/ultra/.files/bin/tg-ctl run` — i.e. the exact same tg-ctl daemon. `launchctl list` shows it loaded with the live pid.

But `composeStatus` only checks for tg-ctl's OWN `enable` mechanism — the unit file `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agenttools.tg-ctl.tg-ctl.plist`. That file is absent (the daemon was never enabled via `tg-ctl enable`; it's wired through the external rig-managed launchd job instead). So status prints:

```
autostart: NOT enabled — run `tg-ctl enable` to start at login
```

while launchd keeps the daemon alive across reboots. Misleading: the CTO sees "not enabled" when it actually autostarts on boot. Two agents flagged it.

## Expected

`status`'s autostart detection should ALSO recognize an external launchd job that supervises this tg-ctl binary (in addition to tg-ctl's own enable mechanism). When such a loaded job is found, report:

```
autostart: enabled (via launchd: ai.hyperide.tg-ctl)
```

## Constraints

- Don't break the own-mechanism (`com.agenttools.tg-ctl.tg-ctl` / systemd unit) detection.
- Discover the supervising label by what it RUNS (the tg-ctl binary), not by brittle-hardcoding `ai.hyperide.tg-ctl`.
- Non-macOS (no `launchctl`) → fall back to the existing logic, never crash.
- Read-only; no daemon restart needed.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests (mock the launchctl/plist probe): autostart ENABLED via external launchd when a loaded job runs this tg-ctl; NOT enabled when neither mechanism exists; own-mechanism still works; non-macOS graceful (no probe, no crash).
- `bun test` green.
- Live: `tg-ctl status` shows the launchd-managed autostart line.

title: tg-ctl: cleanExit unlinks the pidfile unconditionally — a departing/loser daemon deletes the live winner's pidfile (false 'not running')
body:
## Bug

`runDaemon`'s `cleanExit(code)` (tg-ctl, the daemon entrypoint) unlinks the pidfile **unconditionally**:

```ts
const cleanExit = (code: number): never => {
  try { unlinkSync(ctx.paths.pid) } catch {}   // <-- no ownership check
  try { hookServer?.close() } catch {}
  try { unlinkSync(ctx.paths.socket) } catch {}
  process.exit(code)
}
```

It never checks that the pidfile's content is THIS process's own pid. Under a **launchd relaunch** (KeepAlive restart, `enable` re-run, or any window where a second instance overlaps the first) a daemon that is shutting down — or whose ownership was taken over by a newer instance that already rewrote `tg-ctl.<bot>.pid` with its own pid — runs `cleanExit` on SIGTERM/idle-exit and deletes the **live winner's** pidfile.

## Consequence (daily-critical)

`tg-ctl status` / `composeStatus` reads the pidfile; with the file gone it reports **"not running"** even though the real daemon is alive and long-polling. The flock (the true singleton) is unaffected, so routing keeps working — but the operator sees a false negative and may `start`/`enable` redundantly. tg-cli is a daily lifeline; a false "not running" is a real operational hazard.

## Root cause

`cleanExit`'s `unlinkSync(ctx.paths.pid)` is owner-blind. The flock LOSER path (`process.exit(0)` before `cleanExit` is defined) is already safe, but the WINNER's `cleanExit` — invoked on SIGTERM, SIGINT (1947-1948) and idle-exit (3843) — deletes whatever pid is on disk, including a successor's.

## Fix

Only the instance that actually OWNS the pidfile may remove it on exit:
- set an `ownsPidFile` flag (or compare `readPidFile(pidfile) === process.pid`) so `cleanExit` unlinks the pidfile **only when its content is our own pid**;
- the flock loser exits without touching shared state (already true);
- the legit graceful-exit cleanup (winner removes ITS pidfile) is preserved.

Mirrors the existing `unlinkIfOwner` ownership pattern in `features/tg-ctl/routes.ts`.

## RED-first test

Simulate: winner writes pid + holds the flock; a second (loser) instance starts, loses the flock, exits; assert the winner's pidfile SURVIVES. Plus: the winner's own graceful SIGTERM DOES remove its pidfile. And a unit-level check that `cleanExit`-style unlink leaves a foreign pidfile intact.

title: tg --file report.html renders RAW HTML tags in PDF instead of formatted output
body:
## Symptom `tg --file ~/.moshi/uploads/tg-report.html` produced `tg-report.html.pdf` showing **literal HTML tags** as monospace text — ``, ``, ``, `<div>`, etc. sticking out as source — instead of bold/code/table/heading **formatting**. The CTO sends Telegram-subset HTML reports (``, ``, ``, `

`, `
`, `
    `) expecting them rendered. Proof: the broken artifact `~/.moshi/uploads/tg-report.html.pdf` (every tag visible verbatim). ## Root cause `.html`/`.htm` are in `CODE_EXT_LANG` (`features/code-pdf/convert.ts`, `html: 'html'`). So an attached `.html` file matches `isConvertibleCode` → `convertCodeToPdf` **fences the entire HTML content into a markdown code block** (`fenceContent`) and runs pandoc syntax-highlighting. Result: the HTML is shown as *source code*, not rendered as DOM. The code-fence path (meant for `.ts`/`.json`/`.yaml` source files Telegram iOS previews poorly) was wrongly applied to HTML that is meant to be *rendered*. ## Fix An attached `.html`/`.htm` file must be **rendered** to a formatted PDF (HTML→PDF: pandoc `-f html` → standalone html5 → Chrome print-to-pdf) so the Telegram-allowed tags become real formatting (bold/italic/headings/tables/lists/code blocks/blockquotes), NOT fenced as code. Keep the code/config→syntax-highlighted-PDF path intact for real source files (`.ts`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.py`, …). ## Acceptance - A known HTML report string rendered through the HTML→PDF path yields formatted output: no ``/`

`/`

` literal tag substrings leak into the intermediate render, and the bold/heading/table structure is present. - Full `bun test ./tests` green. - Regenerate the report PDF as proof — formatting correct, no raw tags.

title: AskUserQuestion forwards a duplicate Telegram card; second tap reads as 'expired'
body:
## Symptom

An agent's `AskUserQuestion` is forwarded to Telegram as an inline-button card. After the CTO taps an answer (which DOES reach the harness), a SECOND identical card appears. Tapping that second card yields an "expired" toast, reading as "answer not accepted" — even though the first tap already landed.

## Root cause

The `requestId` is a STABLE hash of (session, question text). The in-flight dedup (`activeButtonKeys`) only guards CONCURRENT duplicates and is RELEASED the instant the question is answered.

Two compounding causes:

1. **Double coverage.** Claude Code installs `PreToolUse:AskUserQuestion` AND a `PermissionRequest:*` catch-all. BOTH fire for an `AskUserQuestion`, normalize to the SAME requestId, and forward. (`features/tg-ctl/hook-install.ts:36-37`.)
2. **No idempotency across the answer boundary.** Once the first card is answered, the dedup key is freed; the same `AskUserQuestion` re-firing posts a SECOND card. Proven from daemon logs: the same requestId forwarded twice, 37s apart.

## Fix

- **A** — record answered requests in an `answeredButtons` TTL map; on a re-forward of an already-answered requestId, REPLAY the stored answer down the socket and post NO second card.
- **B** — in `hook-normalize`, drop the `AskUserQuestion` payload delivered via the `PermissionRequest` matcher (only the dedicated `PreToolUse` matcher forwards it).
- **C** — log the answer (currently silent), change the tap toast to "sent to the agent", and reply "already answered" (not "expired") when a tap finds an already-answered key.

## Acceptance

- A re-forwarded already-answered requestId replays the stored answer and posts no new card (daemon integration test).
- An `AskUserQuestion` payload with `hook_event_name === 'PermissionRequest'` normalizes to null.
- Full tg-cli suite green.

title: tg-ctl: question-answer state must survive socket-close + daemon restart (late-deliver + lossless reconnect)
body:
## Problem

The tg-ctl daemon holds all forwarded-question state ONLY in memory (`pendingButtons`, `activeButtonKeys`, `answeredButtons`). Two consequences hurt the CTO's question channel:

1. **Late tap dropped.** When a forwarded question's hook socket closes (the agent's 120s hook budget elapses, or the agent process dies), the daemon deletes the pending entry and edits the card to "expired — answer in terminal". A Telegram tap that arrives AFTER that hits the `!pending` branch and is DROPPED — the CTO presses a button and nothing reaches the harness.

2. **Daemon restart loses everything.** SIGTERM → `cleanExit(0)` wipes every Map. A restart (crash-relaunch by launchd, or a deliberate stop+start) loses all in-flight + recently-answered questions: the reconnecting `tg-ctl ask` client gets null and the human's pending card is orphaned, or a re-fire posts a duplicate card.

## Fix (one mechanism)

- **Persist** scoped questions + the answered-replay cache to a JSON file (`ctx.paths.questions`, atomic write), restore on daemon bootstrap.
- **Late-deliver**: a tap with no live pending socket injects the chosen option into the asking tmux pane (reusing the text-reply injection path) instead of dropping.
- **Reconnect**: the `tg-ctl ask` client reconnects + resends the same requestId on a mid-block socket error/close; the restored daemon re-attaches the pending entry (no duplicate card) or replays the stored answer.
- **UX**: clear the inline keyboard on a genuinely-dead (unscoped/no-pane) expiry.

## Acceptance

- persist→restore round-trip test
- a tap after the pending socket closed → injected to the pane (not dropped)
- reconnect-and-resend across a simulated daemon bounce → no duplicate card / answer replayed
- the existing #98 answered-replay tests still pass

title: tg-ctl late-delivery: verify pane IDENTITY (not just liveness) before injecting a late answer
body:
Follow-up from the #99 review.

`lateDeliverAbandonedQuestion` injects the chosen option into `retained.req.paneId` after verifying (via the inject plan's `verify-pane` step) that the pane still hosts AN agent — but NOT that it is the SAME session/agent that asked the question. Within the retention window (`TG_CTL_ABANDONED_RETAIN_MS`, default 30 min) the user could have started a different task in that pane, so a late tap would deliver e.g. `Production` to the wrong agent.

Blast radius is bounded: the answer arrives as a clearly-attributed `[TG from tg] <label>` inbound message, not a silent wrong action, so a mismatched agent sees an out-of-context message rather than executing something. Still worth hardening.

Options:
- compare the pane's CURRENT agent pid / cwd against the retained `req.cwd` before injecting, and skip (toast 'session changed — answer in terminal') on mismatch;
- or shorten the default retention window.

Not blocking #99 (the late tap reaching the right pane in the common case is the high-value fix); this closes the residual repurpose gap.

title: md-pdf: convertMdToPdf lacks the network-blackhole + drops embed-resources hardening that convertHtmlToPdf got in #96
body: ## What is wrong `convertMdToPdf` (features/md-pdf/convert.ts) renders attached markdown to PDF via pandoc → headless Chrome, but it MISSES the security hardening the sibling `convertHtmlToPdf` path received in #96: 1. **No network blackhole.** Its Chrome `--print-to-pdf` invocation has NO `--host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND`. A markdown report with a remote image (`![x](http://host/p.png)`) makes Chrome FETCH it at print time — SSRF / tracking-pixel / network egress from the user's machine. 2. **`--embed-resources` reads arbitrary local files.** pandoc is invoked with `--embed-resources --resource-path `, which base64-inlines ANY local file the markdown references (`![x](/etc/passwd)`, `![x](../secret)`) into the PDF that is then uploaded to Telegram — a local-file-exfiltration surface. #96 fixed exactly this for the `.html` render path: `printToPdf` carries the DNS blackhole and `convertHtmlToPdf` deliberately omits `--embed-resources` (see the note in features/code-pdf/convert.ts ending 'Follow-up: reconcile md-pdf's broader embed surface — tracked separately'). This issue IS that follow-up. ## Fix (parity with convertHtmlToPdf) - Route convertMdToPdf's Chrome print through the same hardened `printToPdf` helper (single source of the print sandbox flags incl. the DNS blackhole), so the md path can never again silently diverge from the hardened code-pdf paths. - Drop `--embed-resources` + `--resource-path` from convertMdToPdf's pandoc args (same decision #96 made for the HTML path). Accepted cost: a relative LOCAL `` in markdown shows broken; remote images are blackholed anyway. Reports are text, not image documents. ## Acceptance - convertMdToPdf's Chrome argv contains `--host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND`. - convertMdToPdf's pandoc argv contains NO `--embed-resources`. - A real md→PDF render of a doc referencing a local secret file does NOT embed the secret's bytes; a remote image is not fetched. - Legit Cyrillic+emoji markdown still renders to a valid PDF. Ref: agent-tools task #58 (flagged by the #96 HTML→PDF agent).

title: pdf-render: Chrome still loads absolute-path / file:// subresources into the printed PDF (both md-pdf and html-report paths)
body: ## Residual after #102 / #96 Both `convertMdToPdf` (md-pdf) and `convertHtmlToPdf` (code-pdf) render by feeding a local `doc.html` to headless Chrome over a `file://` URL. #102 and #96 closed the pandoc-stage auto-inlining (`--embed-resources` removed) and the remote-fetch surface (DNS blackhole). But a residual remains: **Chrome itself loads an ABSOLUTE-path or `file:`-scheme subresource from the file:// document and prints it into the PDF**, which is then uploaded to Telegram. The DNS blackhole does not apply to `file://` (no host resolution). Verified empirically: a doc with `` (a valid PNG) renders the image into the print-to-pdf output (rasterized PDF showed the image's pixels). So an attacker-authored markdown/HTML report with `` or `` can read a known-path local image into the uploaded PDF. A RELATIVE ref is safe (it resolves into the temp dir, where the file isn't). The realistic exposure is low (requires a known absolute path to an image-decodable file, and the source is the user's own attachment in the common case), but it is a real local-file-disclosure vector and should be closed for the adversarial-input case. ## Fix options - Sanitize the HTML handed to Chrome: strip / neutralize `src`/`href`/`poster`/etc. whose value is an absolute path (`/...`) or a `file:`-scheme URL, in a SHARED helper applied before `printToPdf` on BOTH render paths (so they don't diverge). Keep relative refs (already safe / broken). - Or render the main document from a non-`file://` origin (data: / stdin) so file:// subresources become cross-origin and are blocked — but this also blocks the legitimate external CSS ``, so it needs the CSS inlined first. More invasive. ## Acceptance - A render of a doc referencing an absolute-path / `file://` local image does NOT print that image into the PDF (rasterize-and-check, or assert the ref is scrubbed from doc.html). - Both md-pdf and html-report paths covered by the same mechanism. - Relative refs and the external CSS still work. Found during #102 review (the md→PDF security-parity fix).

title: convertMdToPdf does not sanitize pandoc raw-HTML output — a hostile .md with <iframe src=file://>/<script> reaches Chrome (md path not at .html sanitization parity)
body: ## Gap (surfaced by the #102 review) #102 added the DNS blackhole and dropped `--embed-resources` on the md→PDF path. But the sibling `.html` report path (`convertHtmlToPdf`, #95/#96) does MORE that the md path does not mirror: it runs `sanitizeReportHtml` (strips whole `` executes during the print (`scriptEnabled=false` is intentionally not set — it silently breaks Chrome's print). So the #102 claim of "the same security posture as the .html path" is not yet true. #102 closed the two surfaces it named (network egress + pandoc-stage inlining); this issue tracks bringing the md path to the .html path's element/handler sanitization. ## Fix - Relocate `sanitizeReportHtml` + `stripEventHandlerAttrs` to a shared module (they live in `features/code-pdf/convert.ts`; the md path can't import from code-pdf without a cycle — same relocation pattern used for `printToPdf` in #102), and apply them on the md path: LAYER 1 on the raw `.md`'s HTML before pandoc and/or LAYER 2 on pandoc's `doc.html` output before `printToPdf`. - Combine with #103 (scrub absolute / `file:`-scheme subresource refs) for a complete render-sandbox shared by both paths. ## Acceptance - A `.md` containing `

title: Fix tg review-visual hook timeout and dirty-cwd routing
body:
## What
Ensure tg's pre-send-photo review-visual hook runs review --visual as an image-only gate from a neutral cwd, with a timeout budget that lets review-cli return a structured verdict instead of host-killing the hook.

## Why (motivation)
The TG hook was timing out at 55 seconds and fail-opening, which means screenshots could be sent after a broken or incomplete visual review.

## User impact
Outgoing Telegram screenshots get a real visual gate result instead of a silent fail-open timeout.

## Cost of inaction
The same warning will keep appearing on TG sends, and visual proof discipline remains unenforced in the channel where screenshots are delivered.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] pre_send_photo.py runs review from a neutral non-git temporary cwd so dirty repos cannot route the photo hook into full diff review. — forced: Source and installed hook now run subprocess.run(..., cwd=tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='tg-review-visual-')); regression test 'review visual hook runs review from neutral non-git cwd' passes.
- [x] The installed descriptor timeout is longer than the hook-owned review timeout, and AGENTS_HOOKS_TRUST=1 pins are updated. — forced: Installed descriptor timeout_ms is 180000, hook-owned REVIEW_TIMEOUT_S is 175 seconds, and AGENTS_HOOKS_TRUST=1 tg hooks trust review-visual refreshed trust.json pin.
- [x] A regression test proves the hook uses neutral cwd, and a live hook invocation on evolve-hyperide-threaded-v4.png returns allow without timeout. — forced: bun test tests/hooks-review-descriptor.test.ts passed; live /Users/ultra/.agents/hooks/tg/pre_send_photo.py invocation on /Users/ultra/xp/rig-cli/evolve-hyperide-threaded-v4.png returned {'hook_api':'agents-hooks/v1','decision':'allow'} without timeout.

## Screenshots
(none)

## Links
- Session: session:35

## Skipped gates
- screenshots: Hook/runtime infrastructure fix; proof is hook output and regression tests.

title: Notify Telegram when the harness hits a session limit or API error; inline button schedules auto-continue at reset time
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Alex (tg#5698, verbatim): «Сделай ещё чтобы когда у харнеса исчерпывается сессия или происходит ошибка чтобы это прилетало в тг. А ещё если известно когда лимиты обновятся чтобы в тг была кнопка автоматически продолжить по на наступлении времени». Today a Claude Code session that dies on 'You have hit your session limit · resets 4:10am (Europe/Belgrade)' or an API error is SILENT: no tg signal, the operator discovers the dead session hours later. Claude Code 2.1.x ships a StopFailure hook event (matchers: rate_limit, overloaded, billing_error, ...) that fires when a turn ends on an API failure; the exact failure text (incl. the reset time) is present in the transcript as a synthetic assistant message.

## User impact
Operator learns about a limit-stopped or errored agent immediately on the phone and can one-tap schedule an automatic continue injection at the known reset time instead of losing hours of idle night time.

## Cost of inaction
Limit-stopped agents keep dying silently; goals stall overnight; the operator must poll tmux manually.

## Acceptance criteria
