title: Scheduled usage push: a send failure on the boundary day loses the report, next day's retry is a wrong-cause notice
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
review-cli (Opus, correctness role) found this while reviewing an unrelated PR merge (tg-cli PR #229, https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/229) that pulled in features/tg-ctl/usage-schedule.ts as catch-up content from an already-merged feature (tg-cli PR #292, https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/292, issue #290, https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/290). On a boundary day (Sunday or month-end), if rig usage composes successfully but the Telegram send fails (a 5xx response, a timeout, a transient error), the composed report body is dropped entirely -- the loop just continues to the next period. The next day's check sees the period still due, but the on-time flag is now false since the boundary day has already passed, so it emits the missed-report notice claiming the machine was asleep or off at 23:50 -- a factually wrong cause for what was actually a transient send failure -- and the real numbers are gone for good, because rig usage can only report the CURRENT period, never a past one. This directly contradicts the feature's own changelog claim that a failed send or compose leaves the period due and gets retried: the retry does happen, but it can never reproduce the report, only a misleading notice. The interactive daily-report command in the same original diff already solved exactly this class of problem via a persisted pending-report file (compose succeeds, send fails, the body is saved and prepended to the next successful send) -- this ticket is to apply that same, already-proven pattern to the scheduled usage push.

## User impact
the scheduled weekly/monthly usage report, the feature's whole reason to exist, silently loses its data on any transient Telegram error on the boundary day, then tells the user a wrong story about why, undermining trust in the notice text for every other real machine-was-asleep case too.

## Cost of inaction
the gap ships permanently in the exact scenario it will eventually hit (a transient network or API blip during the once-a-week or once-a-month send), and the misleading notice text will cost time diagnosing a phantom sleep or power issue that never happened.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] a boundary-day compose success followed by a send failure persists the composed report body (mirroring the daily-report pending-file pattern) instead of discarding it
- [ ] the next scheduled check sends the persisted report first when present, rather than emitting the missed-report notice's wrong 'machine was asleep' text for a report that was actually composed and just failed to send
- [ ] a regression test covers: compose succeeds, send fails, next-day check delivers the original report content, not a missed-notice

title: tg-ctl: migrate the legacy Codex hooks.json Stop entry away, detect the telemetry hook in config.toml, and recognize the launchd-owned daemon in status
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Follow-ups left open by [issue #308](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/308) and [PR #200](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/200). rig now provisions the Codex usage-telemetry Stop hook into the Codex config.toml, but tg-ctl only ever SKIPPED writing hooks.json — it never removed the legacy entry, so Codex kept printing 'loading hooks from both hooks.json and config.toml' until Alex deleted the file by hand (backup kept at hooks.json.pre-308-migration.bak). status still reads only hooks.json, so it claims the telemetry hook is NOT installed while it is live in config.toml; and it reads only the pidfile, so it claims the daemon is not running while the launchd-owned ai.hyperide.tg-ctl instance (pid 11062, uptime 1d6h) is alive.

## User impact
Alex sees a Codex startup warning on every session until he hand-edits config files, and `tg-ctl status` — the one command that is supposed to answer 'is my bot alive and are my hooks wired' — lies on two of its lines at once: it says the telemetry collector is missing and says the daemon is down, while both are actually fine.

## Cost of inaction
Every new machine (and every re-run of install-hooks) recreates the dual hook source and the warning, and status stays untrustworthy — so nobody can tell a real outage from a reporting bug without running launchctl and grepping two config files by hand, which is exactly what this investigation had to do.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `tg-ctl install-hooks` removes the legacy `tg-ctl codex-usage-hook` Stop entry from the Codex hooks.json file when the same hook is already provisioned in the Codex config.toml [hooks] table — backing the file up first, deleting hooks.json when nothing else is left in it, printing exactly what it did, and printing a 'nothing to migrate' line on every later run (idempotent).
- [ ] `tg-ctl status` reports the Codex usage telemetry hook as installed when it lives in config.toml, falling back to the legacy hooks.json, and names which of the two files it was found in.
- [ ] `tg-ctl status` reports the daemon as 'running (launchd, pid N)' when a launchd LaunchAgent supervises it, 'running (manual, pid N)' for a hand-started daemon, and still reports a stale pidfile as stale — with the launchd detection strictly read-only (no live service mutation of any kind).

title: Approval requests report "not posted" for messages Telegram actually received
body:
## What
When an agent asks Alex for a one-time approval, the asking side reports back "ask-forward not-posted ... daemon declined or unreachable" and the approval is denied. For one request on 2026-09-05 the daemon log at ~/.config/tg-cli/launchd.tg-ctl.err.log line 3567 records the opposite: "ask-forward posted ... messageId=14880" at 19:46:35.513Z. The message reached Telegram; the agent was told it had not. Two further problems ride along. The card expired at 19:48:25.229Z, 110 seconds after posting, with no human decision. And every request raised from a codex session logs agent=claude with subagent, window and pane all empty, so there is no route back to the agent that asked.

## Why (motivation)
The client and the daemon disagree about what counts as a successful post, and the client treats its own timeout as proof of non-delivery. Separately the ask is capped well below the time a person needs to notice and answer a phone notification.

## User impact
Alex gets a Telegram card asking him to approve something, taps nothing within two minutes because he is doing something else, and the agent is told the message was never sent. The agent then stops, reports the approval transport as broken, and the work Alex asked for does not happen. Six times over two days on 2026-09-05/06.

## Cost of inaction
Every guard that routes its exception through Telegram is effectively deny-only, so agents stop asking and either stop or find a way around the guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When the daemon records a posted messageId, the asking side never reports the request as not posted.
- [ ] An approval card stays answerable for long enough that a person can realistically respond, and an expiry is reported as an expiry rather than as a delivery failure.
- [ ] A request raised from a codex session records the real harness and enough routing detail to deliver the answer back.

title: tg-ctl: control live omp via ACP, not tmux send-keys
body:
## What
tg-ctl can recognize omp in tmux (https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/243) but inbound Telegram still only injects via tmux send-keys. An omp session outside tmux is merely listed unreachable and queued to a Stop-hook inbox (https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/306). omp 18.1.14 speaks ACP over stdio (initialize, session/new, session/prompt) and NDJSON RPC (type:prompt with message). Telegram text, session title, and harness questions must go through that live API. Never omp --resume --print (https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/322 forks history). When a tmux pane AND the API both exist, use the API only. Tmux discovery must still classify kind=omp so mixed setups stay visible.

## Why (motivation)
Alex 2026-09-07: harnesses that can be controlled without tmux must work without it; omp in Telegram must actually work (replies, user messages, names from the harness). 2026-09-08 addendum: if omp is also in tmux there must be no send-keys conflict — talk to omp directly. Closed 243 is recognition only, not live inject.

## User impact
You message an omp session from Telegram and nothing reaches the live agent unless it sits in tmux; even then the text is typed into the TUI as keystrokes, which collides with whoever is using the pane. Questions never become Telegram buttons. Sessions are labelled by cwd guess instead of omp's own title, so /agent routing is guesswork.

## Cost of inaction
omp stays a second-class harness in Telegram: outside tmux you wait for the next turn's inbox; inside tmux a tap or message can type into the wrong prompt. The resume --print approach on https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/322 is unsafe to merge.

title: CI gates fail closed and audit PR lockfiles as data
body:
## What
The vendored GitHub Actions drop-ins in this repo still have the fail-open bugs already fixed upstream in agent-tools (https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/129, https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/130, https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/131, https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/65). CodeQL language detect pipes git ls-files into grep -q and can skip a language on SIGPIPE. leftover-grep can pass after scanning nothing when the merge-base is missing. secret-scan uses gitleaks-action which demands an org license. dep-audit audits the runner instead of the PR tree and can execute Python sdists under pull_request_target. review-threads can stay stale-green after a later review thread appears. An incomplete rescue of only dep-audit.sh plus an unrelated test already landed in https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/321 (DO NOT MERGE). This ticket covers the full leftover CI/workflow/script diffs currently dirty on the live primary checkout.

## Why (motivation)
A required CI check that silently skips is worse than no check: PRs merge with a green status while CodeQL never ran, leftover markers were not scanned, or Python dependencies were never audited. The live tg-cli primary also cannot keep these diffs: it is the deployed binary and must stay on main.

## User impact
If you open a pull request against tg-cli, GitHub can show a green leftover-grep or CodeQL check even though the gate scanned nothing or skipped a language. A secret scan can fail for license reasons rather than for a leak. A dependency audit can look at the GitHub runner's packages instead of yours, or worse run a malicious setup.py from the PR. Review threads added after the first green check can be merged through the GitHub UI because the required status never flipped red.

## Cost of inaction
Security and hygiene gates keep lying. Vulnerable or leftover-laden PRs merge. Operators are tempted to disable the gates. The live primary checkout stays dirty with this work sitting next to the deployed tg binary.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CodeQL language detect materializes git ls-files first, treats SIGPIPE/grep errors as fail-closed, and does not skip a language that has source in the tree. Proof: the detect step in .github/workflows/codeql.yml plus a targeted read of that step.
- [ ] leftover-grep fails closed when an explicit LEFTOVER_BASE does not resolve or the added-lines diff cannot be computed, and the workflow fetches enough history for a merge-base. Proof: ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh and .github/workflows/leftover-grep.yml.
- [ ] secret-scan runs a version-pinned gitleaks OSS binary via gitleaks dir, not gitleaks-action. Proof: .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml.
- [ ] dep-audit.sh accepts AUDIT_DIR, classifies requirements files, and only runs pip-audit --no-deps -r on pinned specs (unsafe/unpinned fail closed). Proof: ci/dependency-review/dep-audit.sh and the pull_request_target workflow that passes the PR-head side worktree.
- [ ] review-threads re-runs on pull_request_review / pull_request_review_comment and pins checkout to the PR base so the required status cannot stay stale-green. Proof: .github/workflows/review-threads.yml.

## Screenshots
(none)

## Links
- (none)

## Skipped gates
- links: False positives: file paths (ci/leftover-grep/leftover-grep.sh, ci/dependency-review/dep-audit.sh, .github/workflows/*) and the gitleaks/gitleaks-action action slug are not GitHub repos/tickets. Real related issues are already full URLs.

title: pre-send-photo consumes a live Telegram hatch approval without weakening the default block
body:
## What
pre_send_photo.py hard-blocks an unstyled/broken/blank render. That default must stay. A live Telegram hatch approval already given for one send currently has no code path in this hook, so the block still fires (the gap that https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/321 tried to test without shipping the implementation). Add a per-send bypass only when RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_PRE_SEND_PHOTO is set: the hook requests approval via agenttools_hatch_escalation and waits on tg-ctl ask. Unset env keeps the unconditional block. Raise the descriptor timeout_ms to 420000 so the Python process can return its own allow/block before the outer on_error:open kill fail-opens. Default block-on-broken-render is unchanged; this only ADDS the opt-in live bypass (narrowed Option C, not a general warn-only downgrade like https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/163).

## Why (motivation)
An operator can already live-approve a screenshot over Telegram and still lose the send because this hook cannot consume that approval. The tempting wrong fix is to downgrade the veto to warn-only for every send, which removes the only safety net for a genuinely broken render.

## User impact
When you try to send a screenshot that the visual review flags, even after you already tapped approve on the hatch card in Telegram, the photo still does not go out. You see a block, have no supported way to use the approval you just gave, and either drop the proof or start looking for a way to turn the gate off.

## Cost of inaction
Approved visual proofs stay blocked. People pressure to weaken the default hard block for all sends. The implementation and its tests sit dirty on the live primary checkout, or the tests ship without the hook change as in https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/321.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With no hatch request, an unstyled/broken/blank verdict still BLOCKS whether the hatch module is importable or not (regression-safe default). Proof: tests/hooks-photo-hatch-escalation.test.ts cases (a) and (a2).
- [ ] A valid live hatch approval ALLOWS that one send; a denied approval still BLOCKS and surfaces the denial reason. Proof: the same test file cases (b) and the denied-approval case.
- [ ] An approval granted for one send does not leak into a later send that never requested one. Proof: test case (c) in tests/hooks-photo-hatch-escalation.test.ts.
- [ ] Descriptor timeout_ms is 420000 and HATCH_ASK_TIMEOUT_S stays under that budget so a no-response hatch cannot fail-open via on_error:open. Proof: features/hooks/review-descriptor/review-visual.pre-send-photo.json and the HATCH_ASK_TIMEOUT_S constant in pre_send_photo.py.

title: Commit SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 in .ship-config
body:
## What
tg-cli origin/main has no repo-root .ship-config. After https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/609, a committed SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 line on the PR BASE branch is the durable ops off-switch for ship's zero-GitHub-reviews gate (read from origin/<base>, never from the shipping PR's own HEAD — a same-PR commit cannot grant itself the waiver). Evidence captured now: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/229 is MERGEABLE, CI green, review-cli quorum 3/3, but gh pr view --json reviews returns []. git show origin/main:.ship-config fails (path does not exist). Alex said SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW was meant to be off; the env-var form is the leaky anti-pattern from https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/528.

## Why (motivation)
Without a committed .ship-config on main, every tg-cli gh ship of a PR with no GitHub-side review is refused even when review-cli quorum is already 3/3. The intended off-switch only takes effect after a normal merge to main (chicken-egg close). A machine-wide SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 export is being removed and must not be the standing policy.

## User impact
Agents and the maintainer cannot merge already-reviewed, CI-green tg-cli PRs such as https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/229. The send-path bugs stay unshipped: a missing disk attachment still kills the whole Telegram send, and a too-long message can still flood the recipient. End users keep hitting those failures while the merge is blocked on an empty GitHub reviews array.

## Cost of inaction
https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/229 stays open. Future tg-cli ships keep failing the ZERO GitHub reviews gate. Operators keep exporting SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 in the shell, which is the exact leak that broke agent-tools' own gate tests in https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/528, and that env off-switch is being deleted.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] origin/main contains a repo-root .ship-config whose only key is SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0. Proof: git show origin/main:.ship-config prints that line and nothing else.
- [ ] After that line is on main, gh ship of https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/229 is not refused for ZERO GitHub reviews. Proof: the PR is merged, or the exact remaining ship refusal is quoted.

title: Block outbound tg send that mentions screenshot/скриншот without an attached image
body:
## What
tg currently lets an outbound send through when the text mentions a screenshot but no image is attached.

Concrete gap: `tg "see screenshot foo.png"` (no --photo) reaches the transmitter and attempts sendMessage. Observed 2026-09-08 against https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli at the live checkout:

- `tg --dry-run "see screenshot foo.png"` exits 0 and prints: "tg --dry-run: OK — message is well-formed ... see screenshot foo.png"
- `tg "see screenshot foo.png"` with fake creds + TG_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:57193 fails at https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/blob/main/features/transport/telegram.ts sendMessage (ConnectionRefused) — the screenshot gate never fired.

The send path already knows attached photos (`items` from parseArgs, type photo|document) before the cjk-guard / dry-run short-circuit in the https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/blob/main/tg entrypoint. Caption+photo (`tg --photo x.png "screenshot of …"`) already has a file and must be allowed.

Intended: if the caption or --title mentions screenshot or скриншот (any case) AND no photo/image is attached, hard-block (exit 1) BEFORE transmit. The error must tell the sender to attach the image with `tg --photo` / equivalent, and must NOT suggest dodging by deleting the word — attach the screenshot.

## Why (motivation)
Agents keep reporting see-screenshot as text-only Telegram messages. The recipient cannot see the proof. The current CLI has no gate for this, so a missing --photo is silent until a human asks for the image.

## User impact
When an agent says it took a screenshot but only sends the word, you open Telegram and see a claim with no picture. You cannot verify the UI, you have to ask again, and the proof is useless. The fix stops that send and tells the agent to attach the image instead of quietly dropping the word screenshot.

## Cost of inaction
Agents will keep sending screenshot claims without the image. Every such message wastes a round-trip, and visual-proof discipline stays unenforceable at the send boundary.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Bare mention without an image is blocked: tg "see screenshot foo.png" (no --photo) exits 1 before transmit; stderr tells the sender to attach the image with tg --photo / equivalent and must not tell them to delete the word. Proof: CLI test on the real tg entrypoint with fake creds (no network). — forced: CLI/logic gate with no visual surface; proven by bun test tests/screenshot-guard-cli.test.ts and tests/screenshot-guard.test.ts (all 11 tests pass) plus PR https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/338
- [x] Mention plus a real photo is allowed: tg --photo x.png "screenshot of …" does not fire this gate (send may then fail offline/network, but stderr must not contain the screenshot-attach error). Proof: CLI test with a tiny PNG fixture. — forced: CLI/logic gate with no visual surface; proven by bun test tests/screenshot-guard-cli.test.ts and tests/screenshot-guard.test.ts (all 11 tests pass) plus PR https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/338
- [x] Case-insensitive English screenshot and Cyrillic скриншот both trigger the block when no photo is attached. Proof: unit tests on the pure detector plus CLI coverage of both words. — forced: CLI/logic gate with no visual surface; proven by bun test tests/screenshot-guard-cli.test.ts and tests/screenshot-guard.test.ts (all 11 tests pass) plus PR https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/338

title: tg-ctl ACP initialize times out: omp 18.1.14 speaks NDJSON, not Content-Length
body:
## What
Telegram /agent → live omp still fails with `ACP initialize timed out` (15s) at tg-ctl ensureOmpAcp. encodeAcpFrame in features/tg-ctl/omp.ts sends LSP-style Content-Length JSON-RPC; decodeAcpFrames waits for a blank-line Content-Length header and only treats NDJSON as a stray line after `\n\n`. A throwaway `/opt/homebrew/bin/omp acp --no-session --allow-home --cwd=/tmp` child (omp 18.1.14) proves: NDJSON `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",...}\n` returns a JSON-RPC result on stdout (`id` number 1, protocolVersion 1, agentInfo.name oh-my-pi); the same initialize wrapped as Content-Length makes the child exit 0 with empty stdout and empty stderr. That is the timeout: omp never replies, pumpAcpClient never resolves. Response id is a number when we send a number (pump's `typeof rec.id === "number"` is fine on the live path). Spawn argv `--cwd=/tmp` vs `--cwd` `/tmp` both work. Do not sleep-as-fix. Follow-up to https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/323 and merged https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/325 https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/340.

## Why (motivation)
https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/323 shipped ACP control and https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/340 shipped out-of-tmux reply routing, but the stdio framing was assumed to be Content-Length (tests even round-trip it and the fake omp servers speak it). Live omp 18.1.14 `/opt/homebrew/bin/omp acp` is NDJSON JSON-RPC. Every Telegram tap that calls ensureOmpAcp hits the 15s initialize timeout, so /agent and replies never reach omp.

## User impact
You pick an omp session in Telegram (/agent tap, a reply, or inbound text) and nothing happens for 15 seconds, then the bot reports that ACP initialize timed out. The live omp TUI never sees your message. You cannot drive omp from Telegram even though the session is listed.

## Cost of inaction
Telegram→omp stays dead after the ACP work in https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/323 and https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/340. Users keep hitting the timeout; agents may paper over it with sleep or tmux send-keys, both forbidden.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Throwaway `/opt/homebrew/bin/omp acp --no-session --allow-home` child: NDJSON initialize returns a JSON-RPC result (not a timeout); Content-Length still does not. Proof: captured stdout of the child. — proof: ![proof](/tmp/pr346-proofs/acp-initialize-stdout.txt)
- [x] A unit/integration test injects initialize against a fake ACP server that speaks NDJSON only (TMUX unset). A client helper using encodeAcpFrame/decodeAcpFrames completes initialize without waiting 15s. The test fails if initialize never completes (short timeout). Proof: named bun test run. — proof: ![proof](/tmp/pr346-proofs/bun-ctl-omp-acp-unit.txt)
- [x] encodeAcpFrame emits NDJSON (JSON + newline, not Content-Length). decodeAcpFrames parses NDJSON lines so pumpAcpClient/acpCall in tg-ctl resolve initialize. Fake omp servers in tests speak the real framing. Proof: unit test plus integration fakes. — proof: ![proof](/tmp/pr346-proofs/bun-ctl-omp-acp-unit.txt)

title: tg-ctl must self-register OS autostart on first run
body:
## What
ROADMAP asked that on first launch the tg-ctl daemon installs a boot or login autostart entry so it survives reboots: macOS LaunchAgent, Linux systemd user, no-op elsewhere. Idempotent and removable. Today OS autostart is an explicit enable command only. https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/blob/main/features/tg-ctl/autostart.ts#L1-L10 is the pure half of enable and disable. The dispatcher runs enable only when the command is enable. start and run do not write the LaunchAgent. https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/88 (done) only taught status to detect an external launchd job; it did not add first-run self-register. Broken command today: a first tg-ctl start on a machine with no LaunchAgent leaves autostart not enabled; a reboot drops the daemon. Origin: https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

## Why (motivation)
The daemon is how Telegram reaches agents. If it only stays up after a human remembers tg-ctl enable, a reboot silently kills inbound until someone notices. First-run self-register is the difference between a tool that survives login and one that does not.

## User impact
You start tg-ctl, it works, you reboot, and Telegram stops reaching agents. status then says the daemon is down and autostart is not enabled. You have to remember enable by hand.

## Cost of inaction
Every reboot still drops inbound Telegram until someone runs enable, which is the exact outage the ROADMAP item exists to prevent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The first tg-ctl start or run on a machine with no own autostart unit writes the LaunchAgent (macOS) or systemd user unit (Linux with systemd) and status then reports autostart enabled. Re-running start does not duplicate the unit file. Proof: status output plus a single plist or unit file.
- [ ] tg-ctl disable still removes autostart, and a host with no supported OS autostart does not pretend it enabled. Proof: disable then status, plus a documented no-op path.

title: tg-ctl drops RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* Telegram approvals when the human taps after the requesting process exits
body:
## What
agent-tools' agenttools_hatch_escalation.request_hatch_approval pipes a manually-built ButtonRequest of kind 'permission' into 'tg-ctl ask' over stdin for every RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* escalation. Because this is a headless, one-shot request (no live tmux hook, no per-invocation harness normalization), the request always has paneId: undefined and promptTurnId: undefined. In tg-ctl, retainAbandonedQuestion (~line 3104) does 'if (!req.paneId) return false' unconditionally, so the moment the requesting tg-ctl ask process's socket closes (its own client-side timeout, or the harness killing it) — which routinely happens before a human has tapped the Telegram button — the pending entry is expired (expireDeadCard) and dropped from rt.abandoned entirely, never retained. A human tap that lands even a moment later has no live card/entry to land on: the approval is silently lost. This is the ONLY delivery path any RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* approval currently has (agent-tools makes zero other changes), so this is not a corner case — it is the single mechanism, broken for the common case of a slow human tap.

## Why (motivation)
Alex (product) explicitly flagged this: queued Approve for rig -- this daemon can't prove a later reconnect is the SAME request, so it won't auto-deliver; you'll need to tap again... a decision must not be silently lost even when expired -- instead relay to the agent that the user approved, set a flag/marker allowing one retry, and tell it the exact command plus a caveat to only use it if still relevant. Root cause verified by reading tg-ctl's retainAbandonedQuestion (around line 3104), armPendingSocketClose (around 3152-3169), handleHookSocketLine (around 3342), the permission tap handler in lateDeliverAbandonedQuestion (around 8438), notifyAbandonedLongOutage (around 5010), and the durable-state restore filter (around 5198), plus features/tg-ctl/questions.ts's ButtonRequest doc comments confirming a hatch request structurally can never populate paneId or promptTurnId.

## User impact
Every human who taps Approve/Deny on a rig hatch-escalation Telegram card slightly slower than the requesting process's own timeout gets silent failure: the agent believes it was denied/never answered, the human believes they approved it, and nothing reconciles the two. This directly undermines trust in the hatch-approval flow, which exists specifically for cases the agent cannot safely proceed on without a human decision.

## Cost of inaction
The RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_* approval channel remains silently unreliable for any tap that isn't near-instant; humans will keep re-approving the same escalation multiple times or giving up, and agents will keep treating a genuinely-approved hatch as denied, defeating the purpose of a human-in-the-loop safety gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A hatch-shaped permission ButtonRequest (kind: permission, paneId undefined, promptTurnId undefined, requestId matching hatch-<hookId>-<12 hex>) whose ask-socket closes BEFORE any Telegram tap is retained (not expired) in tg-ctl's abandoned-button map, keyed so a later tap can still land on it. — forced: Backend/daemon logic fix, no UI surface to screenshot. Proof: tests/ctl-hatch-approval-retry-integration.test.ts all 3 tests pass (junit at /tmp/task-349-proof/hatch-retry-junit.xml): 'HATCH RETRY' proves criteria 1-3 (socket-close retention, durable queuedDecision, automatic retry-answer with same hookId, no new card); 'HATCH ABANDONED' proves criterion 4 (hatch-specific card text, no impossible reconnect/terminal promises); the test file itself is criterion 5's named regression test, verified to fail pre-fix (retainAbandonedQuestion's unconditional !paneId->false) and pass post-fix. Also fixed a second review-finding gap (raw UNSCOPED_ABANDON_MS backstop timer bypassing retention in the default connected-process scenario) with its own new passing test in the same file.

title: ACP session/prompt stays wedged forever after one failed prompt (post-#346)
body:
## What's wrong

Alex reported "ACP session/prompt timed out" errors recurring in Telegram, after
the NDJSON framing fix (#346 / #341) was already merged and live on the deployed
daemon.

## Evidence

From `launchd.tg-ctl.err.log` on 2026-09-09, the SAME session id
(`01a08270-31de-747a-9cad-a004085c0394`, cwd `.../hyperide/packages/state-lib/site`)
timed out 3x over 30 minutes, under a daemon (pid 825, started 07:27:01Z) that
had already loaded the merged NDJSON fix -- initialize and session/load both
logged as succeeding each time:

```
09:27:26.561Z omp-acp: session/load sessionId=01a08270-... cwd=.../state-lib/site pid=20148
09:29:26.563Z omp-acp: prompt failed cwd=.../state-lib/site session=01a08270-...: ACP session/prompt timed out
09:58:00.049Z omp-acp: prompt failed cwd=.../state-lib/site session=01a08270-...: ACP session/prompt timed out
10:00:03.796Z omp-acp: prompt failed cwd=.../state-lib/site session=01a08270-...: ACP session/prompt timed out
```

Live process inspection confirmed the spawned `omp acp` child (pid 61725) stayed
alive 35+ minutes after its first timeout, holding 90+ open sockets -- it was
never killed or evicted after the failed `session/prompt`, so `ompAcpClients`
kept reusing the exact same wedged pipe on every subsequent reply into that
session, repeating the identical failure forever.

## Root cause

`promptOmpAcp` (tg-ctl) caught the `acpCall` timeout/error but never removed the
client from `ompAcpClients` nor killed its process. Confirmed distinct from #346:
that fix made initialize/session-load succeed (visible in the log above); this bug
is entirely in the post-load `session/prompt` failure path.

## Fix

See #352: evict the client from `ompAcpClients` and kill its process on any
`session/prompt` failure, so the next reply spawns a fresh child instead of
reusing a permanently wedged one. Regression test
(`tests/ctl-omp-acp-prompt-evict.test.ts`) red-checked against the pre-fix code.

title: tg-ctl: stale pane registrations survive a tmux server restart (pane_id reuse)
body:
## What
tg-ctl's per-pane registration store (features/tg-ctl/registration-store.ts) keys entries only by tmux's %N pane_id string, and pruneRegistrations() treats an entry as live purely by checking "is this paneId in the current tmux snapshot". tmux's pane_id counter is monotonic only for one continuous tmux server process lifetime: across a server restart (reboot, tmux kill-server, a crash) the counter resets to zero, so a brand-new unrelated pane can be assigned the exact same low %N a long-dead pane from a PRIOR server lifetime once held. Liveness pruning alone cannot tell these apart, so a stale registration.json entry can silently survive forever and route Telegram messages to the wrong, unrelated pane.

## Why (motivation)
Live evidence captured on a production machine: ~/.config/tg-cli/tg-ctl.8574086668.registration.json held two ~2-month-old stale entries (%5 -> /Users/ultra/xp/hyperos, %1 -> /Users/ultra) that tmux had since reassigned to entirely unrelated panes (a status pane and a different agent's pane respectively). discover.ts's pickTargetPaneFromSet() tier 1 trusts a registered-but-stale paneId against live candidates, so a fresh inbound message with no explicit /agent selector can silently route to the wrong session.

## User impact
Without this fix, a user's Telegram message can be silently delivered into the wrong agent session (a different, unrelated project) any time tmux reuses a low pane number across a server restart -- with no error, no visible sign, and no way to detect it except by noticing the reply came from the wrong project.

## Cost of inaction
Registration staleness across a tmux server restart will keep causing intermittent, hard-to-diagnose misrouting of inbound Telegram messages to unrelated agent sessions, worsening as machines accumulate more tmux restarts over their uptime.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] pruneRegistrations drops an entry whose serverEpoch no longer matches the live tmux server epoch, in addition to the existing pane-liveness check
- [ ] Every pre-existing registration (no serverEpoch field) is unaffected and continues to prune by pane-liveness only (verified by unit tests)
- [ ] The live epoch is cached with a bounded TTL, not for the whole process lifetime, so a long-lived daemon does not permanently blackout registrations after a real tmux server restart

title: tg-ctl: ask-forward log line conflates timeout with daemon failure (tg-ctl:3726)
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
On 2026-09-09, this exact log wording sent two separate agents (in different sessions) chasing a phantom tg-ctl daemon-outage investigation for ~40 minutes combined. `tg-ctl status` and the daemon's own append-only log confirmed the daemon was completely healthy the entire time, and every single ask was actually posted successfully to Telegram — the real cause was plain unanswered-within-115s human timeouts, which tg-ctl:3726 phrases identically to a genuine 'daemon declined or unreachable' failure: `log(`ask-forward not-posted: req=${req.requestId} agent=${req.agent} pane=${req.paneId ?? "-"} — daemon declined or unreachable`)`, fired whenever askDaemonOnce() (tg-ctl:3652) returns null for either reason.

## User impact
Every future review-gate or hatch-escalation ask that simply times out waiting on a slow human Telegram reply gets misdiagnosed as a daemon outage by whichever agent next reads this log line, wasting investigation time and eroding trust in the daemon's real health signal (tg-ctl status already proves health correctly — this log line alone is the misleading part).

## Cost of inaction
Agents will keep re-investigating a healthy daemon every time a human is slow to answer on Telegram, repeating the ~40-minute wasted-investigation cycle from 2026-09-09 indefinitely, and the same ambiguity will keep propagating into every downstream consumer of this log (e.g. agent-tools' hatch-escalation library).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] tg-ctl:3726's log() call no longer reuses the single ambiguous 'daemon declined or unreachable' wording for both (a) an ASK_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS (115000ms, defined tg-ctl:3588) unanswered-in-time human timeout and (b) a genuine daemon/transport failure inside askDaemonOnce (tg-ctl:3652). The two cases must produce visibly distinct log text (e.g. an 'ask-unanswered: no reply within 115s (req=... pane=...)' message for the timeout case vs a separate, genuinely-different message for a real connection failure).
- [ ] askDaemonOnce's distinct failure paths (reconnect-dropped vs plain deadline-elapsed) are logged differently, verified by reading the updated call site and confirming both paths. Any other surface that echoes the current wording (e.g. agent-tools' agenttools_hatch_escalation library, tracked separately as an agent-tools issue) is noted as a dependent follow-up.

title: Delivery isolation: preserve per-target ordering without waiting for another agent's response
body:
## Outcome
A hung or busy target does not delay delivery to another target sharing the daemon. State mutations for the same logical target/resource remain ordered. Shortening a prompt timeout is not the definition of delivery isolation.

## Why / user impact
The reported serial action loop awaited an OMP prompt response before continuing, stalling unrelated agents. The user's later clarification in #360 requires sending without waiting for a full agent turn and rejects new timer-based workarounds.

## Parent / specification / dependencies
Parent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/380
Specification: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/blob/docs/ecosystem-grooming-2026-09-10/docs/specs/2026-09-10-telegram-control.md#concurrency-and-route-identity
Related: #360 durable acceptance and #377 generic interactive transport.

## Delivered baseline
PR #362 is recorded as merged at 6a0329a79c0e5c9bcd0368e93507548109f695f5: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/362. It added per-target concurrent dispatch and tests; preserve that work. The prior task reports a /tmp test log and a 15-second timeout clamp. Those are historical implementation/test claims, not a newly performed live acceptance. A timeout clamp is not a required architectural outcome and does not satisfy #360.

## Remaining acceptance criteria
- [ ] Exercise the actual daemon dispatch/poll path with one never-completing target and another healthy target. The second target's delivery and subsequent update polling progress without resolving the first target's model turn.
- [ ] Same-target messages and shared topic/question/button state remain ordered under concurrent batches; record the actual resource-key scheme and multi-resource handling.
- [ ] Concurrency is bounded with explicit saturation behavior; no unbounded process fan-out or untracked background work substitutes for a serial queue.
- [ ] Restart/crash recovery preserves durable accepted operations from #360 and does not send them to a reused target identity.
- [ ] Tests use barriers/controlled fake transports rather than sleep-and-hope scheduling, include cancellation/cleanup, and are retained during #377 migration.
- [ ] Document exact passing integration commands and accepted revisions. Reconcile the existing timeout behavior with #360; do not add a new arbitrary prompt deadline as the solution.

## Priority / closure
P1. This is acceptance/hardening of the existing dispatch work, not an instruction to reimplement it. Keep the issue open until the actual isolation contract is verified; do not infer live behavior solely from helper-level tests.

title: tg-ctl: rescope omp delivery to fire-and-forget, fix offset-advance-before-persistence ordering (supersedes PR 322)
body:
## What
Remove the synchronous omp-resume-and-wait delivery mechanism that [PR #322](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/322) introduced for out-of-tmux omp sessions: /agent <selector> <text> currently calls omp --resume <session file> --print <text> --mode=json and blocks the Telegram bot for up to roughly 55 to 120 seconds awaiting the agent full turn reply before responding. Replace it with fire-and-forget delivery via the existing ACP writeAcp primitive: send the prompt over the session ACP connection and return immediately, the same way tg-ctl already delivers to every other non-blocking harness/route, relying on the harness to surface any reply back through its own normal channel (a human on Telegram is a full substitute for a synchronous agent reply per Alex own description of the feature). Separately, fix a durability-ordering bug in the shared getUpdates poll loop: the Telegram batch offset must only advance after the batch (and each accepted message in it) is durably persisted to local disk, never before, so a SIGTERM or SIGKILL immediately after a message is accepted cannot lose it. Delivery itself stays at least once (a redelivered message after a crash and restart is safe and idempotent to reprocess), it does not need to become exactly once. No new timer, deadline, or expiry mechanism is introduced anywhere in this change. A follow-up PR implementing this corrected design is [PR #359](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/359).

## Why (motivation)
This directly supersedes [PR #322](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/322), which built the wrong thing for the right ticket, [task-cli#138](https://github.com/alex-mextner/task-cli/issues/138). Alex rejected that PR synchronous wait premise outright, quote: PR 322 eto sdelal: bot teper zhdyot do 55 sek nastoyashchiy otvet agenta, bred sumasshedshego, zachem bot chtoto zhdet, pochemu 55 sekund, zachem on zhdet otvet agenta, feature banalnaya, CHELOVEK mozhet otvechat agentu cherez telegu, VSE. English: PR 322 did this, the bot now waits up to 55 sec for the agent real answer, that is insane, why does the bot wait for anything, why 55 seconds, why does it wait for the agent reply, the feature is trivial, a HUMAN can reply to the agent via telegram, THATS IT. He also rejected the queue and wait model generally, quote: ranshe bylo, soobshchenie prosto vstavalo v ochered, kakaya eshchyo ochered, prosto nado otpravlyat, kharnes sam razberyotsya, glavnoe znat kogda v kharnese otkryt tui s voprosom ili zaprosom prav. English: before it was, the message just went into a queue, what queue, you just need to send it, the harness will sort it out, the main thing is knowing when the harness has an open TUI with a question or permission request. This is also a direct application of his standing timer rule, recorded 2026-09-09 in project memory, quote: u bota est taymer bezopasnogo perezapuska, tg-ctl colon 4940, 8 sekund, opyat kakaya to khuynya, nikakikh suka taymerov ne dolzhno byt, taymery eto 99 procent kostyl vsegda krome sluchaev kogda polzovatel prosit taymer. English: the bot has a safe restart timer, tg-ctl line 4940, 8 seconds, that is nonsense again, there should be no timers at all, timers are a workaround 99 percent of the time, always, except when the user asks for one. That PR own synchronous wait was exactly this kind of timer shaped workaround, a 120 second ACP call timeout papering over a design that never needed to wait. The root cause of that PR wrong shape is [task-cli#138](https://github.com/alex-mextner/task-cli/issues/138) itself: its acceptance criteria over scoped Alex actual ask into a literal synchronous contract, quoting that criterion: Sending a Telegram message to that session delivers it and returns the agent reply synchronously, not deferred to next turn, verified live with a real omp session. Alex own motivating quote in that same ticket only asked for bidirectional message passing, quote: otvety na voprosy, otpravka soobshcheniy ot polzovatelya agentu i td. English: answers to questions, sending messages from the user to the agent, etc. Never a blocking full turn reply. That acceptance criteria over scope during ticket drafting is the root cause being corrected here, not a reversal of Alex original ask. Separately, Alex stated the actual durability requirement this ticket also fixes, quote: esli bot prinyal soobshchenie poka on ego ne zapishet v bd on ne dolzhen davat ego ubit po krayney mere pri minus 15 kille. English: once the bot accepts a message, until it writes it to the database, it must not allow itself to be killed, at least on a SIGTERM kill. Related, still valid, unrelated concurrent dispatch fix that also touches promptOmpAcp and will need a trivial rebase once this ticket PR lands, keep it on its own merits: [tg-cli#357](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/357). The corrected-design replacement PR is [PR #359](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/359).

## User impact
Telegram message delivery to every out-of-tmux omp session stops blocking the whole bot process for up to two minutes per message, so a wedged or slow-to-reply agent can no longer stall delivery to every other unrelated agent or user sharing the daemon. And a crash or forced restart occurring immediately after a Telegram message is accepted can never silently drop that message, because the offset that marks it consumed will not advance until it is durably on disk.

## Cost of inaction
That earlier synchronous wait design, or something shaped like it, eventually merges over Alex explicit on the record rejection, forcing a second redo later plus the review cycles already spent on the wrong shape. The latent offset before persistence ordering bug remains in place, meaning a routine restart or crash at the wrong instant can silently and permanently lose a real inbound Telegram message with no redelivery, since Telegram will not resend an update once its offset has been acknowledged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] omp message delivery via writeAcp fire and forget never blocks the Telegram bot on the agent reply, no synchronous wait on any ACP session/prompt call in the delivery path
- [ ] The Telegram getUpdates offset only advances after the corresponding batch is durably persisted to local disk, never before
- [ ] A SIGKILL sent immediately after a message is durably persisted does not lose that message, delivery may be at least once and idempotent on replay, but never silently dropped
- [ ] No new timer based, deadline based, or expiry based workaround is introduced anywhere in this change

title: tg-ctl: active-silence nudge for tg-unaware agent sessions
body:
## What


## Why (motivation)
Alex has repeatedly asked agents to reliably use tg-cli. The tg skill exists and is discoverable via the SessionStart blurb, but its documented triggers (finish a task, hit a question/blocker) only fire at a natural decision point — a long, heads-down working stretch never produces one, so passive skill discovery alone cannot close the gap.

## User impact
Agents that go silent for over an hour lose visibility for Alex. A proactive daemon-side nudge restores that visibility without anyone having to poll the chat, closing the gap the passive skill discovery cannot.

## Cost of inaction
Agents keep silently working for hours with zero Telegram visibility; Alex has no async way to know status, ask a question, or catch a stuck session short of manually checking every pane.

## Acceptance criteria

No UI to screenshot; backend module.

Confirmed in code + tests/tg-awareness-nudge.test.ts covering exactly-once and failed-delivery-stays-due. No UI; backend daemon logic.

## Rework: awareness-nudge sweep now routes through harness-cli's universal live-agent API (no more hand-rolled ACP in tg-cli)

Alex's objection, verbatim: "какой ужас нельзя зашивать в TG никакие конкретные Harness все
должно быть универсально и через адаптеры... За работу с харнесами должен отвечать harness-cli
давай универсальное высокоуровневое api для работы как через cli для людей и агентов так и по
какому-то более подходящему inter process протоколу, в идеале кросс-платформенному." (tg-cli
must not embed any specific-harness knowledge; harness-cli must own ALL harness-specific
knowledge behind a universal, high-level API — a CLI surface for humans/agents, and a more
suitable, ideally cross-platform, inter-process protocol for programmatic callers.)

The original shipped version of this feature (PR #364) hardcoded omp/ACP protocol knowledge
directly into tg-ctl's daemon poll loop — exactly the pattern Alex was objecting to. This
follow-up PR removes that:

- Liveness enumeration and delivery now go through harness-cli's new `harness agents --live
  --json` / `harness nudge AGENT_ID MESSAGE --json` subcommands — harness-cli's universal
  live-agent nudge API — instead of tg-ctl's own `listLiveOmpAgents()` + `promptOmpAcp()`.
- IPC is a documented subprocess+JSON contract over argv/stdout, not a new daemon/socket:
  harness-cli is a one-shot, stdlib-only CLI with zero daemon infrastructure today, and this
  fire-and-forget, at-most-once-per-hour nudge doesn't justify adding one.
- `features/tg-ctl/tg-awareness-nudge.ts` and the poll-loop sweep now import neither
  `promptOmpAcp` nor any ACP protocol type from `features/tg-ctl/omp.ts`. The only omp-aware
  code left in the sweep is a small LOCAL bridge (`listLiveOmpAgents`) that resolves which tmux
  pane/pid a harness-cli `session_id` belongs to, purely to look up tg-ctl's OWN paneId-keyed
  outbound-send history — routing bookkeeping, not harness protocol.
- **Store-key migration**: the awareness-nudge store is now keyed by harness-cli's own agent id
  (`harness:kind:path`) instead of a tmux paneId / `omp:<pid>` synthetic origin — a one-time
  cold-start reset of `tg-ctl.<botid>.awareness-nudge.json` on upgrade (worst case one skipped
  or one extra nudge episode, never a spurious storm).
- Any future harness-cli kind becomes nudgeable with zero further tg-ctl changes: the sweep
  trusts harness-cli's own `nudge_supported` flag per row and never special-cases a `kind`
  string.

**Scope boundary, intentionally NOT touched**: the separate, still-ACP-resident capability of
routing a human's live-typed Telegram reply INTO a running omp session (message injection) and
relaying back `session/request_permission` asks (12h `ABANDONED_PERMISSION_RETAIN_MS` retention)
stays exactly as it was. That's a stateful, latency-sensitive, daemon-resident bidirectional
channel — moving it to harness-cli's current one-shot, no-daemon CLI shape would need real
daemon/socket infrastructure there, a materially bigger decision than this rework's scope.
Tracked as a separate follow-up: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/377

See harness-cli's own universal live-agent nudge API (PR/issue linked from that repo — filed in
parallel by a sibling agent) for the adapter side of this contract.

title: chore: enable worktree-only guard on primary checkout (prevents dirty-stale-primary incidents)
body:
## What

Enroll `agent_hooks.worktree_only: true` (or equivalent enforcement) so agent sessions
cannot make direct edits/commands against a repo's **primary** checkout — only against
worktrees.

## Why

This is the root-cause class behind the fleet-wide review-cli outage: an agent session
worked directly in review-cli's primary checkout, leaving it dirty/stale (uncommitted
changes, stale HEAD), which broke `review diff` / `gh ship` across the whole fleet until
a manual stash+pull+rebase cleanup. A worktree-only guard on the primary checkout
prevents that class of incident from recurring, in tg-cli and elsewhere.

## Acceptance

- Primary checkout enrolls the worktree-only guard (`agent_hooks.worktree_only: true` in
  rig.yaml, or equivalent).
- Direct edit/commit attempts against the primary checkout are blocked/redirected to a
  worktree.

title: tg-ctl: non-reply auto-bind (tg-cli#78 anchor) never applies with 2+ out-of-tmux omp candidates — regression
body:
## What
`resolveLastUserTarget()` (tg-ctl) implements the tg-cli#78 anchor guarantee:
a non-reply inbound message from the CTO auto-binds to the pane of his own
last resolved delivery, and never re-shows the agent picker while that anchor
still resolves to a live candidate. But it only ever sees `TargetPane[]`
candidates from `discoverTarget()` — a **tmux-pane-only** view.

The out-of-tmux omp support added later (#306, #339, #342) reaches a
**separate** fallback branch inside `injectViaTarget()`, gated on
`found.reason === "no-agent"` (zero tmux panes at all). That branch calls
`listAgentCandidates()` — which *does* merge in live omp agents running
outside tmux — but picks purely by `candidates.length`: 1 candidate injects
directly, 2+ candidates **always** call `postRoutePicker(...)`. It never
consults `resolveLastUserTarget` / the `last-user-target.json` anchor at all.

## Why (motivation)


## User impact
Every non-reply follow-up message to a multi-agent, out-of-tmux omp fleet
interrupts the CTO with a picker he already answered moments ago, instead of
silently routing to the agent he is actively working with — exactly the
friction #78 was filed to eliminate.

## Cost of inaction
The out-of-tmux omp path (#306/#339/#342) is becoming the common case, not
the exception, so this regression gets more disruptive as fewer agents run
inside tmux. Every multi-agent non-tmux session pays a picker tap on every
single follow-up message.

title: tg-ctl ask: report the daemon's real posted/dropped/expired outcome instead of a generic not-posted
body:
## What
The daemon now writes an interim status line on the hook socket before its final reply, stating whether the card was posted to Telegram, dropped at the door, or expired unanswered, and tg-ctl ask reads that line to log the real outcome instead of one generic decline message for every non-response. This also covers the hook reconnect/resend path and a resend that lands after the human already answered via a pane reply.

## Why (motivation)
Incident 2026-09-05: an agent asked Alex for a one-time exception; the daemon posted the card to Telegram, nobody tapped within the unscoped window, and the client logged the same generic decline message it uses for a card Telegram never received. The client conflated a request refused at the door with a request that was posted and simply timed out.

## User impact
Alex sees a Telegram approval card and, when he does not answer in time, the agent that asked now correctly understands he saw it but did not respond — instead of wrongly concluding the card was never delivered to his phone and abandoning or working around the approval step.

## Cost of inaction
Every guard that routes its exception through Telegram is effectively deny-only: agents wrongly conclude the approval transport is broken and stop or find a way around the guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] When the daemon records that a request was posted to Telegram (including across a hook reconnect, or a reply that lands after the human already answered another way), the asking side never reports it as not posted. — forced: backend/CLI change, no UI to screenshot; proof is the test run: bun test tests/ctl-ask-forward-truth.test.ts tests/ctl-buttons-integration.test.ts -- 4 pass/0 fail, covering expired-with-messageId (never not-posted), not-registered decline, unreachable, and the reconnect/pane-delivered fixes in ctl-buttons-integration.test.ts

title: tg-ctl ask: a request raised from a codex session has no pane/window/subagent to route an answer back to
body:
## What
HookEnv.paneId/windowName/sessionName are read from process.env.TMUX_PANE and the daemon tmux lookups, and subagent from detectAgentLabel. When the hook process that raised the request is a codex session outside tmux (or where these signals are otherwise unavailable), the forwarded request logs agent=claude with subagent, window and pane all empty, so there is no route back to the session that asked. Needs a codex-specific signal (session id, cwd-based match, or an explicit --session flag on the hook invocation) that survives outside a tmux pane.

## Why (motivation)
Incident 2026-09-05 (tg-cli#317): a codex-raised approval request logged agent=claude with every routing field empty, so even a tapped answer had nowhere concrete to go back to.

## User impact
Alex taps an answer to a codex agent's approval request, and the daemon has no way to confirm which live session actually asked, so the answer cannot be routed back to the agent that is waiting on it.

## Cost of inaction
A codex-raised approval or question is effectively unanswerable through Telegram: the tap has nothing to deliver to, so the agent waits out its timeout and falls back to a terminal prompt nobody is watching.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A permission/question request raised from a codex session records a real, non-empty routing target instead of empty routing fields.
- [ ] A daemon-side answer to a codex-raised request is delivered back to the actual codex session that asked, verified with an integration test that raises a request from a non-tmux codex-shaped hook invocation and confirms delivery.

title: tg-ctl: 3 generic-ask hardening findings from PR #368 review round 3 (not yet fixed)
body:
## Summary
A 3rd `review diff --task 149` round on PR #368 (tg-ctl generic `ask` primitive, tg-cli#149) surfaced 3 additional low/medium findings that were NOT fixed before shipping (deprioritized to unblock the merge; none regress prior behavior).

## Findings
1. **MEDIUM** — An unrecognized-flag truncation warning (`parseGenericAskArgv`'s `warning` field) is only logged to the CALLING SCRIPT's stderr, never shown on the Telegram card itself. An approver can tap Approve on a card whose question was silently shortened (e.g. `tg-ctl ask rm --recursive /prod-data` posts a card reading just "rm").
2. **MEDIUM/LOW** — An empty or whitespace-only question (e.g. `tg-ctl ask --timeout 60` with no positional text) posts an approvable blank Telegram card instead of denying outright before any send.
3. **LOW** — `ButtonRequest.skipPaneDefer` is honored even on a SCOPED (paneId-present) raw-socket request in `paneHasPendingQuestion`; only the sanctioned CLI (`runGenericAsk`, always unscoped) sets it today, but a raw-socket caller sending `skipPaneDefer: true` with a `paneId` could re-open the exact tg#30 paste-into-open-prompt bug the defer exists to prevent.

## Suggested fixes
1/2: In the `tg-ctl ask` dispatch (around `if (cmd === "ask") { if (genericAsk) { ... } }`), deny outright (`exit 1`, clear stderr reason) when `genericAsk.warning` is set (truncation) or `genericAsk.question.trim() === ''`, instead of proceeding to post a card.
3: Guard `skipPaneDefer` to only take effect when `!paneId`, either in `normalizeButtonRequest` or as `if (pb.req.skipPaneDefer && !pb.req.paneId) continue` in `paneHasPendingQuestion`.

## Source
review-cli `--task 149` round 3 (roles: correctness, quality — omp:anthropic/claude-fable-5), full transcript: `review task 149 --detail <iteration>`.

title: test suite: gh ship's local full-suite fallback gate is structurally flaky (4/4 runs failed on unrelated hardcoded-timeout tests)
body:
## Summary
`gh ship`'s local full-suite fallback gate (used when a CI check is a confirmed pre-existing flake via `--known-flake`) failed 4 times in a row while shipping PR #368, each time on a DIFFERENT small subset of unrelated pre-existing integration tests — never the PR's own changed files. This makes the local-fallback path for ANY future `--known-flake` ship attempt unreliable, not just for #368.

## Evidence
4 consecutive `bun test` runs (2921-2924 tests, 175-176 files) on the same machine, no code changes between runs:
- Run 1: ctl-buttons-failure-integration, ctl-unreachable-route-integration, ctl-omp-acp-integration, ctl-daemon-integration, ctl-question-durable-integration
- Run 2: ctl-buttons-failure-integration, ctl-unreachable-route-integration, ctl-multi-question-abandon-integration, ctl-omp-acp-integration, ctl-daemon-integration
- Run 3: ctl-unreachable-route-integration, ctl-multi-question-abandon-integration, ctl-tasks-integration, ctl-omp-acp-integration, ctl-daemon-integration
- Run 4: ctl-unreachable-route-integration, ctl-multi-question-abandon-integration, ctl-omp-acp-integration, ctl-daemon-integration

`ctl-unreachable-route-integration`, `ctl-omp-acp-integration`, and `ctl-daemon-integration` failed in EVERY run; `ctl-multi-question-abandon-integration` in 3/4. Each failure is a hardcoded short assertion timeout (`5000ms`, some `10000-20000ms`) with effectively zero jitter margin — e.g. `ctl-daemon-integration.test.ts:190` (`expect(offsets).toContain(105)`, received `[0]` — an async offset-advance race, not host load) and `ctl-omp-acp-integration.test.ts` / `ctl-unreachable-route-integration.test.ts` (flat 5000ms waits with no retry/backoff headroom).

Retrying after the reporting agent confirmed "fleet load has dropped significantly" did NOT change the outcome (run 4 above), which rules out simple host contention as the sole cause — these specific tests' margins are structurally too tight for a 2900+-test suite's own natural scheduling jitter.

## Suggested fix
Audit `ctl-daemon-integration.test.ts`, `ctl-unreachable-route-integration.test.ts`, `ctl-omp-acp-integration.test.ts`, and `ctl-multi-question-abandon-integration.test.ts` for hardcoded short timeouts/waits and either raise their margins or make the underlying assertions poll-based rather than a single point-in-time check after a fixed delay.

## Context
Discovered while shipping alex-mextner/tg-cli#368 (tg-ctl generic `ask` primitive) via `gh ship --known-flake test` — the CI-side flake was correctly confirmed and passed, but the local fallback then repeatedly refused on unrelated failures. See PR #368's ship attempts.

title: Generic interactive agent control: migrate all message and permission routes to harness-cli
body:
## Outcome
Telegram can send a human message and relay a permission decision to the correct live native session through one generic harness API. Tg-cli contains no ACP framing, OMP-specific session discovery or provider-specific permission protocol after the migration.

## Why / user impact
Alex explicitly requested harness-specific behavior to live behind harness-cli adapters. The awareness-nudge migration is only one path; retaining a separate interactive OMP client forces every future harness to require bespoke tg-cli changes.

## Parent / specification / producer dependency
Parent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/380
Specification: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/blob/docs/ecosystem-grooming-2026-09-10/docs/specs/2026-09-10-telegram-control.md#generic-interactive-transport-migration
Producer: https://github.com/alex-mextner/harness-cli/issues/22
Shared identity/inventory: https://github.com/alex-mextner/harness-cli/issues/26
Related: #360 durable acceptance, #357 target isolation, #373 headless origin, #379 stale nudge targets.

## Existing implementation to migrate
`features/tg-ctl/omp.ts` defines ACP types, method names and discovery. Inventory all `ensureOmpAcp`, `ompAcpClients`, `promptOmpAcp` and `replyOmpAcpPermission` call sites at the implementation revision; the earlier count of approximately eight is a baseline, not a coverage target.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Record and review the producer's persistent IPC ownership and cross-platform binding before implementation. A subprocess-per-nudge path alone does not satisfy the interactive lifecycle.
- [ ] A call-site matrix maps every direct message, reply, /agent selection, topic route, deferred delivery, permission request and permission reply to the new generic operation.
- [ ] Submit/recover intent without waiting for full agent-turn completion; accepted, delivered, completed and unknown are distinct adapter results. A successful pipe write alone is not a proven receipt.
- [ ] Native session generation, request IDs and exact decision scope survive transport reconnect/restart; a new session or different action cannot consume an old permission.
- [ ] Preserve the existing 12-hour abandoned-permission retention behavior and wedged-client recovery tests, adapting them to the new transport rather than deleting them. No new arbitrary expiry workaround is introduced.
- [ ] A failed target does not block unrelated targets; same-target state changes stay ordered and pending decisions survive child eviction.
- [ ] Remove the old consumer-owned ACP engine only after parity tests pass. A second/fake adapter exercises the same Telegram paths without new harness-specific branches.
- [ ] Attach producer/consumer revision pairs, reproducible integration results and separately authorized live acceptance. Nudge-only or producer-only evidence cannot close this task.

## Priority / boundaries
P1. Keep Telegram transport in tg-cli and harness protocols in harness-cli. No live daemon restart, real approval card or account change is part of this grooming.

title: tg-ctl: awareness-nudge sweep repeatedly fails with 'Internal error' for stale /private/tmp omp ACP sessions
body:
## What
The tg-ctl daemon's active-silence awareness-nudge sweep (features/tg-ctl/tg-awareness-nudge.ts, [tg-cli#363](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/issues/363)) repeatedly logs 'omp-acp: prompt failed cwd=/private/tmp session=<uuid>: Internal error' followed by 'awareness-nudge failed for %11: Internal error' / '%12: Internal error' on a roughly 50s cadence in the live production daemon log (/Users/ultra/.config/tg-cli/tg-ctl.8574086668.log). Observed continuously across at least two daemon restarts on 2026-09-10 (before and after [PR #371](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/371)/[PR #378](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/378)), for the same two session ids/panes (%11, %12) pointed at cwd=/private/tmp -- these look like orphaned/stale omp ACP sessions the sweep keeps retrying against instead of giving up or pruning them.

## Why (motivation)
Discovered incidentally while verifying production daemon health after shipping [PR #371](https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/pull/371) -- the noise makes the daemon log harder to scan for real issues and suggests the awareness-nudge sweep has no backoff/pruning for a session that has gone permanently stale.

## User impact
Someone reading the bot's log to see if anything is wrong has to wade through an endless stream of the same repeated error about two long-gone sessions, so a real, brand-new problem is easy to miss in the flood.

## Cost of inaction
The log keeps accumulating an unbounded stream of identical noise for every stale session forever, and a genuinely NEW daemon error is easier to miss in the middle of it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The awareness-nudge sweep no longer logs a repeating 'Internal error' for a stale/dead omp ACP session on every sweep cycle -- either the session is pruned from the sweep set after a bounded number of consecutive failures, or the failure is downgraded to a single one-time log line instead of a per-sweep repeat.
- [ ] A regression test covers the stale-session case: the sweep encountering a prompt failure for a session that no longer resolves to a live pane/process does not retry it forever.

## Screenshots
(none)

## Links
- (none)

## Skipped gates
- screenshots: Backend service log noise, no UI surface to screenshot.

title: [EPIC] Reliable Telegram agent control: durable delivery, generic harness API and scoped approvals
body:
## Outcome
Every accepted Telegram message has a durable, correctly routed outcome without blocking unrelated agents. Decisions survive a slow human or a client disconnect, but may authorize only the exact request the human reviewed. All harness-specific protocol logic lives behind harness-cli adapters.

## Parent and specification
Parent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/rig-cli/issues/514
Specification: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/blob/docs/ecosystem-grooming-2026-09-10/docs/specs/2026-09-10-telegram-control.md

## Child work / priority
- [ ] P1 #377 — persistent interactive transport migration, paired with https://github.com/alex-mextner/harness-cli/issues/22.
- [ ] P1 #360 — durable-before-ack, fire-and-forget delivery; completion of an agent turn must not hold the Telegram poll loop.
- [ ] P1 #357 — cross-agent concurrency and strict ordering within a target.
- [ ] P1 #379 — stop repeatedly nudging definitively dead/stale sessions; distinguish unknown from live.
- [ ] P1 #373 — preserve an originating non-tmux session's reply route through the generic adapter contract.
- [ ] P0 #374 — reject blank/truncated approval requests and retain the pane pending-question guard.
- [ ] P1 #354 — tmux generation-aware route identity; a reused pane ID is not the original agent.
- [ ] P1 #375 — deterministic lifecycle/concurrency tests, not increased sleeps.
- [ ] P2 #356 — queryable, correlated hatch history.
- [ ] P2 #344 — declared autostart behavior that respects explicit disable and shared service ownership.

## Existing fixes to preserve
#372 / PR #370 implements posted/dropped/expired reporting. #349 / PR #376 implements late hatch retention; exact-action replay scope still needs independent negative validation. #369 / PR #378 fixes the multi-candidate headless anchor; its truncated acceptance text needs repair, not automatic reopening. #363's awareness nudge is only one consumer, not completion of all harness migration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Persist inbound intent and routing context before advancing the Telegram offset; restart replay is at-least-once with idempotent acceptance/deduplication.
- [ ] An unrelated target continues progressing while another target's harness is busy or fails; same-target ordering is deterministic.
- [ ] accepted, delivered, completed, failed and unknown are not conflated; a write to a pipe alone is not proven delivery.
- [ ] Late approvals are durable and one-use, bound to request/action/scope identity; changing command, repository or origin cannot reuse them.
- [ ] The existing pending-permission retention contract survives migration; no new arbitrary deadline/expiry workaround is added against #360's instruction.
- [ ] tg-cli contains no ACP method/framing/account-path knowledge after migration; generic contract fixtures cover a second adapter and unsupported capabilities.
- [ ] Fault-injection tests cover disconnect-before-tap, crash-before/after-persist, duplicate update, stale pane/session, wedged child and teardown without orphan processes.

## Closure and boundaries
P0/P1 work precedes UI polish. The implementation is not part of this grooming. Do not restart the operator's live daemon, send real approval cards, rotate credentials or kill live agents during documentation/fixture verification.
